-Sand mining ear Badonkalan is taking place in huge amounts. This location is close to Goraghat-Dabra highway

- We were waiting near highway looking for a lift, and saw many tractors pass by - some of which were empty and some with sand

- Most tractors did not give us lift

- Finally sat in a tractor to go near River Sindh from BadonKalan village

- On the way, at one place, the tractor stopped, and the driver went to a cabin / house like structure and came back

- Many tractors were stopping on the way at this point from both ways

- Alluvial ravines on both sides

- After a point there was a bifurcation in road, one led to the BadonKalan village, but the tractor took the other route which went deeper in the alluvial ravines and it was a Kaccha road, it was a difficult route from within the ravine slopes. On this route only the people involved in sand and morram mining were seen.

- It was suspicious and scary and we decided to get down from the tractor before even reaching the river and walked all the way back. We were also unsure of the connectivity to walk further, as many locals had warned us it might be difficult to go further from that point.

- In google maps, this point on river shows mining over the years, some temporary sand bridges (pipa puls), trucks, tracks on sand, temporary sand bunds, changing river flow, disappearing sand formations, algae formation

- Datia DSR 2022 mentions 3 mining sites in BadonKalan (BadonKalan - D, A, E - of areas 23, 23, 24.094 Ha respectively)

- Comparing Datia DSR 2022 and other DSRs of districts from which River Sindh flows, we found that BadonKalan is the biggest mining site on River Sindh.

Sprawling site just upriver from Bardhamann city. Spoke to 2 sand miners (freelance)

Been working at this site for more than 15 years. Pay is about 1000-2000 per day for working till 3pm. They manually dig sand from flooded areas with perforated buckets; they load those onto small mechanized boats that then take it to the other side and deposit it for the excavators, who then presumably load it onto trucks. These two miners have been working this site for about 15 years, and consider it a very profitable enterprise.


We observed boats with suction heads attached by pipes to some central vacuum and cleaner that deposits the sand in piles. These are the ones that likely cause the perfectly round or oval depressions we see


Second interviewee (a local not involved with mining) said mining doesn't stop in the monsoon.

In 2017, the SC restrained 82 lease holders from carrying out sand and bajri mining in Rajasthan. The court will now hold the first hearing regarding this case. The centrally empowered committee appointed by the apex court has already made the recommendation of issuing environmental clearances to valid LOI holders.
Despite the Supreme Court ban, illegal sand mining continues in Ajmer with the mining and police departments turning a blind eye to the problem.

The state Government allowed three large leaseholders to restart mining bear luni and banas river bed. These leaseholders have received the environmental clearance. In 2017 the SC restrained 82 leaseholders in the state to do sand mining this created a crisis in the real estate sector as both consumers and constructors had to buy sand illegaly at a very high price.

After 4 years the SC gave nod to sand mining in the river beds of Rajasthan. The apex court initially constituted a Centrally Empowered Committee to look into the matters of illegal sand mining in Rajasthan.
Four labourers, including a woman, have died after a sand dune collapsed on them during illegal sand mining operations in Rajasthan's Bundi district.

Sarpanch Raghuvir Meena had gone to conduct a raid at Hindpura village near Sawai Madhopur, accompanied by police and officials of mine department, when a mob attacked the entire team and the Sarpanch was beaten to death.
The Rajasthan ACB unearthed a major sand mining rakcet operating from Manoharpur police station in Jaipur.

The mines and mineral departmen has imposed stringent measures to combat illegal mining and transportation of sand in the state. Previously the penalty stood at a minimum of 1.25 lakh but now under the new regulations it has been increased upto 3 lakhs.

Two persons involved in transporting of illegaly mined sand were killed, while four others including two pilice constables were injured during a fierce shoot-out between the police and mining mafia in Dholpur's Basai Dang village.

Officials from the revenue departmen, mines, police ,RTO joined forces in crackdown on sand smugglers operating around the narmada river in Vadodara district. Karjan police seized 50 vehicles for violating traffic rules. 35 sand dumpers wereseized by the RTO and memos were issued, imposing a fine of  rupees 4,38,500 on spot.

A 45-year-old man was shot dead over dispute related to sand mining in Chhota Udepur region at Gujarat.
According to complainant, Zabeer Rathwa, villagers of Motikanas village and Khadakwada village close to Madhya Pradesh-Gujarat border in Chhota Udepur have been at loggerheads with each other regarding the limits of the river bed of Orsnag river, cutting through both the villages.

This article dwells on the impact of illegal sand mining in the region of bharuch. Although sand mining is legal in some cases, illegal sand mining has become a widespread problem in many regions, including Bharuch. Illegal sand mining is a criminal activity that involves the removal of sand from riverbeds without proper authorization or permits and environment clearance.
The consequences of illegal sand mining in the Narmada River district of Bharuch are manifold. Firstly, it has led to severe ecological damage, resulting in the loss of biodiversity and wildlife habitats. The sand mining process disturbs the natural riverbed, resulting in the destruction of aquatic vegetation, which is the habitat for several aquatic species. This can also lead to the loss of fish stocks, which are an important source of food for local communities.

Farmers of forty villages out of about one hundred villages in Meval region met and resolved to stop sand mining in the region. About three hundred of them stated that the indiscriminate sand mining had destroyed the rivers in the region and as a result the water level of the wells has gone down, the big Mango and Mahua trees had dried up and the villagers were forced to migrate in search of livelihood. Criticizing the role of the elected representatives like MLA, MP, Pradhan etc. they said that they are not concerned with the problem. On the contrary some of them have themselves been involved in sand mining.

Despite orders from NGT and SC upholding it, the Jaipur district administration is yet to recover penalty of over 13 crore levied on 134 persons accused of illegal sand mining. The penalty had been levied by the NGT and upheld by the apex court. The amount is to be used to replenish and rejuvenate the area that has been ransacked by the illegal miners and build roads that have been damaged while transporting sand.
Four persons, including two children, killed when an illegal sand mine collapsed in Madhya Pradesh's Shivpuri district.

Sand mining resumed in Alappad in the Kolam district in Kerala despite local protests. The protests were the result of negative sea sand washing impacts such as land loss through erosion, and damage to coastal embankments, among others.

The new CRZ map, prepared by the expert team appointed by MoEF on September 27, 2018 emphasised on the critical vulnerable area in CRZ area which pose threat to fish breeding, affects coral reefs and other marine bio-diversities. The map forbids any sort of sand extraction activities in entire Kundapur taluk which also includes Byndoor.
People complain that illegal sand mining is going on day and night in Boko region of Kamrup District in Assam. Two river dolphins are claimed to have died due to this illegal sand mining.

Illegal machine operated sand mining along the banks of the Kopili and Borpani rivers in Nagaon district of Assam. The news highlight thatr around 200-300 sand trucks ply everyday through that route from which the officials get commision.
Udupi District In-charge Minister Jayamala has expressed displeasure over the district administration’s failure to solve the row over shortage of sand.
Police in Karnataka's Chamarajanagar seized two trucks in a raid at an illegal sand mining spot near Cauvery river belt at the Kollegal taluk of the district.

The Dakshina Kannada district administration has decided not to appeal against a High Court order, allowing unregulated sand extraction from the Phalguni and Netravathi rivers in the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ). They have issued permits to 202 traditional sand extractors, despite a previous ruling by the NGT stating that selling sand extracted from CRZ rivers constitutes commercial mining, which is prohibited. Environmentalists were relieved by the original order, as it aimed to protect the river beds from excessive extraction. However, the sand extractors challenged the order in court, resulting in its dismissal on the grounds that it only applied to Udupi district, not Dakshina Kannada. The administration has now restored permits for 148 individuals and issued 54 new permits, risking the delicate coastal ecology.

The Dakshina Kannada district administration has granted temporary permits for traditional sand mining in the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) of rivers within the district. Deputy Commissioner Ravikumar M.R., serving as the chairman of the District CRZ Committee, issued orders approving permits for 54 individuals and communities who applied to engage in traditional sand mining. These permits will allow them to extract sand from the dunes in the CRZ areas of Phalguni and Nethravati rivers. The decision follows a ruling in May by the National Green Tribunal's Southern Bench in Chennai, which halted large-scale commercial sand extraction along the Karnataka coast. According to the NGT's order, only the local community using traditional methods can remove sand bars, and sand can only be extracted for the safe passage of fishing boats. The sale of extracted sand is prohibited, but it can be used for nourishing beaches, river beds, or river banks.

Deputy Commissioner Ravikumar M.R. announced in a press conference that a seven-member committee will convene on November 14 to address the sand shortage in Dakshina Kannada district. Discussions will focus on both legal and illegal sand mining and transportation, with the aim of curbing illegal activities by ensuring proper regulation of legal mining. In Udupi district, the National Green Tribunal had previously banned sand excavation in CRZ limits, a decision which was later overturned by the high court following a challenge from sand mining contractors. Instead of pursuing a higher appeal, the district administration plans to explore traditional methods of sand excavation.

In Assam, 04 people have died in 03 road accidents involving sand transporting vehicles in 11 months. These accidents happened while the transporting of sand via trucks in both Golghat and Kamrup districts of Assam. In another, the crushing down of a political worker by a speeding sand dumper in Udharbond area of Cachar district on January 1, 2023, turned into a violent incident in which angry mob battered and burnt down the dumper.

Deputy Commissioner Dr. Rajendra K V banned sand mining in Dakshina Kannada district based on a National Green Tribunal (NGT) order that prohibited sand mining in Udupi district's coastal regulation zone (CRZ) limits. However, sand miners challenged the ban in the high court, which temporarily stayed the ban. In response to the NGT's ban on sand mining in the CRZ limits of Udupi, traditional sand miners from Udupi filed a petition in the Supreme Court. They argue that the sand mining industry has been operating for five decades, providing livelihoods to thousands of people, and that if sand mining is not allowed, it will lead to the accumulation of sand near river mouths, affecting fishing and causing artificial floods. The sand miners' association plans to appeal to the Supreme Court to permit sand mining in CRZ limits. The high court has supported the sand miners' association's stance and stayed the ban imposed by the Deputy Commissioner of Dakshina Kannada.
Karnataka Lokayukta police raided various sites in Dakshina Kannada district where illegal sand mining was allegedly going on and confiscated assets worth Rs 40 lakh, including vehicles.

The recent floods in Uttara Kanada district has come as a godsend for illegal sand lifters in Joida taluk. Sand-laden trucks from the taluk, which have become a common feature, are quietly sent to other parts of the state. Despite many checkposts, such trucks are having a free run as police, officials and revenue officials have been turning a blind eye.

Karnataka is a leading state that witnesses the devastating effects of sand mining.

Senior officers of the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) rushed to Yamuna bank to dismantle a mysterious road that had cropped up on the river. The move came a day after Hindustan Times had reported about the path under the Delhi Metro bridge between Yamuna Bank and Indraprastha.

A sub-divisional magistrate with the Delhi government has written to an executive engineer in the DJB, alleging that a licensed company has been routinely lifting more sand from the Yamuna riverbed at Sonia Vihar than it can under the licence conditions.

Vijayapura district in India has a history of criminal activities, earning it a reputation as the land of killers. Now, the district faces a new challenge: the sand mafia. Despite a ban on sand mining by the Green Tribunal, illegal activities continue in the Krishna and Bhimanadi rivers. District Collector YS Patil Khadak has taken action to combat this issue. A meeting was held with officials from various departments, and instructions were given to control illegal mining and closely monitor transportation. To address the problem specifically in the Indi taluk area, two officers have been assigned round-the-clock duty, and a task force committee has been established. Immediate action will be taken on complaints, with coordination from the police department. Negligence and lack of coordination will result in appropriate action against officials involved.

Persistent illegal sand and gravel mining in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh, threatens one of the two known Indian winter habitats of black-necked cranes that fly in from Tibet at the end of every year. District authorities in Arunachal Pradesh are passing the buck on the matter.
Uncontrolled mining of sand and gravel from river beds and agricultural lands has assumed an alarming proportion in the hill district of Karbi Anglong.
Illegal sand mining on Brahmaputra river bed is posing serious threat to eastern Assam’s Dibrugarh town protection dyke.

The Assam Police's Bureau of Investigation has arrested a deputy ranger of Golaghat forest division for his involvement in an illegal sand mining racket in the Doigrung river area of Golaghat district.

In a drive against the illegal traders conducted at Sonaikuchi, Kamalajari and Jugadal areas, a team of forest officials seized as many as 9 trucks loaded with sand which were illegally mined. They have been digging out sands from cultivable fields while others are mining the Digaru River by using machines illegally.

Rameshwar Teli, BJP MP from Dibrugarh constituency, wrote a letter to the Divisional Forest Officer of Digboi, directing him to allow illegal sand mining in Ushapur area under Digboi forest division in Tinsukia district.

Sand mining operation has been temporarily suspended in four units across Hailakandi district of Assam  following a probe.

The Mines and Mineral Department officials of Valsad carried out raids at Valsad Nagar Palika-run water works and found that illegal sand mining activities were going on there.The officials demanded documents from a person present at the spot, Kalidas Mangela, who failed to submit the necessary papers following which they seized six pipes, two boats, and other equipment, all worth Rs 3 lakh.

Mines and Earth Sciences Minister Murugesh Nirani announced in the Legislative Assembly that a new sand policy will be implemented in Karnataka to benefit the rural and common people. Under the policy, sand will be provided at a rate of Rs. 100 to Rs. 200 per ton for constructing houses within 10 lakhs. The government aims to address the issue of expensive sand, making it accessible to the poor. The minister emphasized the convenience of the policy, which will cover construction projects from Gram Panchayats to municipal councils. Strict action will be taken against illegal sand transportation, and measures are being taken to prevent leakages in sand mining revenue. MLAs raised concerns about the sale of filtered soil as sand, the seizure of bullock carts by the police, and the involvement of officials in illegal activities. Minister Nirani assured that the issues would be addressed and resolved.

Yogesh Savjani (27), mines supervisor in the geology and mining department of Chhota Udepur district was attacked by a group of 15 people, he sustained severe head injuries, while one of the security guards accompanying him was injured as well.
NGT directs inquiry into alleged illegal mining in Dehing Patkai Wildlife Sanctuary and the Makum Pani Reserved Forest in Digboi, Assam.
Leader of the Opposition in Assam Debabrata Saikia requested forest minister Pramila Rani Brahma to take steps to curb alleged rampant illegal mining in Sivasagar district.

Assam’s Kulshi river, one of the few remaining habitats of the endangered Ganges river dolphins, is under threat. A prominent southern tributary of the river Brahmaputra, the Kulshi river is quietly bearing the brunt of unplanned urban development. Unscientific mining has triggered erosion on the either banks at various parts. Pressure on the river is alarmingly on the rise due to its sand quality and growing demand of sand. Drastic depletion of water level, dying water flow, water pollution and dwindling fish population have sounded the death knell of the river’s prized possession, dolphin, world’s most endangered mammal.

Illegal sand trading is thriving in Bidar's Manjra River, benefitting both Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Exploiting the river's dry state caused by the rains, sand is being transported day and night without any hindrance. Shockingly, the police are allegedly involved in this illicit trade, allowing sand to be sold openly. Vehicles without number plates pass right in front of the police station, carrying sand and engaging in looting activities. The unauthorized transportation of sand is occurring without permits in some areas. Tractors, trucks, and even Hitachis are employed to remove substantial amounts of sand from the river. Despite its significant impact on groundwater and the sleepless nights caused by constant sand transportation, law enforcement and government officials have turned a blind eye. Local residents are demanding immediate action to address the scarcity of drinking water and the environmental repercussions of this ongoing issue.
In a drive against illegal sand mining, a team led by Sonapur Forest Ranger Gautam Mahanta demolished five sand-mining sites in the Dimoria.

Although land mafias are siphoning crores of rupees from the government's exchequer by stealing illegal plain sand from Sabarmati river bed, there is no concrete and permanent action by the mining and mineral sector. Anger has spread among the villagers as the sand mafia in Lekawada Sabarmati river has been excavated beyond limits and thousands of metric tons have been lifted and turned into huge pits. In spite of repeated complaints in this matter and resolution in the Gram Panchayat to boycott the election, there is no permanent stop to the activities of illegal sand mining.

Mallika Sarabhai writes to the Geology and Mining Commissioner over illegal mining in Fatepura, near Pethapur in Gandhinagar. In her letter to the Commissioner of Industry and Mines, Sarabhai stated “the river is being raped” as sand pits have been dug to a depth of about 40 feet.

Activists of Thoubal River Conservation Committee intercepted nine trucks transporting sand and stones scooped from the riverbed in Thoubal district of Manipur and forced the drivers to dump the same.
DFO Thoubal bans Sand Mining At Thoubal River. The DFO also orders ban transportation of red sand in Thoubal and Kakching district.

A Dalit man named Deepak Makwana who is also the President of Rashtriya Dalit Adhikar Manch was attacked by two upper caste men named Rama Boliya and Lala Boliya for apparently seeking a lease for sand mining. They shouted casteist slurs at him and snatched away his gold chain saying that a Dalit shouldn't wear gold.
A 4-year-old boy was buried alive under sand when an earth leveling machine dumped sand on him by mistake.

City-based environmentalists have alleged that rampant illegal sand mining is being carried out between Belapur and Kharghar near the creek during night time. The environmentalists have also intimated the Raigad district authorities about the same.

Scam of illegal sand mining using duplicate royalty pass was unearthed by the Mines and Minerals Department of the Chhota Udepur district. Police said that the scam was to load sand from any lease or non-lease area in the district and then issue a forged royalty pass so that there will not be any hurdles from the mines and minerals department.

বালি পাচার চক্রের বিরুদ্ধে কড়া পদক্ষেপের সওয়াল করলেন রাজ্যেরা জল সম্পদ উন্নয়নমন্ত্রী মানস ভুঁইয়া( Manas Bhunia)। মঙ্গলবার মেদিনীপুরে এসে এ বিষয়ে পুলিশ ও প্রশাসনকে কড়া পদক্ষেপ করার নির্দেশ দিয়েছেন তিনি।
Rampant sand smuggling continues through the city highways of Guwahati showing higher levels of corruption among those monitoring the system.

Illegal sand mining along the coast of Kharghar, near Morbi village, has come to light, said environmentalists. Activists pointed out that the mangroves have been partially destroyed by sand miners who dump debris in the CRZ area in order to encroach it.

The entire mangrove stretch between Kharghar and Mansarovar is in constant danger from land sharks and those who indulge in illegal sand mining.  Mangroves are deliberately destroyed so that suction pumps can be setup to take out the sand from this coastal region.

A large potion of the riverbed, in the Kharghar section of the Taloja river, has been affected by sand-mining activities. The traditional fishermen in the vicinity, dependent on the river for their daily catch, pointed out that in spite of numerous complaints, neither government officials nor local police officers have taken any action to contain the sand mafia working in the belt. Large portions of mangroves and the natural flow of the Taloja river have fallen prey to sledging and dredging activities taking place in broad daylight.
The State Revenue Department set on fire 45 fibre boats used by the sand mafia for illegal dredging along the Vaitarna river in Virar.

At least eight people were killed while making crude bombs that were being rushed to rival groups locked in a turf war over illegal sand mining in West Bengal . The incident took place at Tarka village in Birbhum district .
Sand mining at Mahim Causeway is once again raising concern among residents and environmentalists, who say the illegal activity puts lives at risk and is also harmful to the ecosystem.

বালিপাচার রুখতে পথে TMC কাউন্সিলর। Asansol Municipality র ৩৮ নম্বর ওয়ার্ডের কাউন্সিলর Mina Kumari Hansda র অভিযোগ, বালিপাচারের জেরে ক্ষতিগ্রস্ত হচ্ছে রাস্তা ও জলের পাইপলাইন। ডামরা এলাকায় বালিপাচার রুখতে পথে নেমেছেন কাউন্সিলর ও তৃণমূলের স্থানীয় নেতারা। প্রশাসন তৎপর না হলে জেলাজুড়ে আন্দোলনের হুঁশিয়ারি তৃণমূল কাউন্সিলরের।
[TMC councilors on the way to prevent sandblasting. Councilor Mina Kumari Hansda of Ward No. 38 of Asansol Municipality complained that roads and water pipelines are being damaged due to sand mining. Councilors and local leaders of Trinamool have come to the road to stop sandblasting in Damra area. The Trinamool councilor has warned of agitation across the district if the administration does not take action.]

An illegal sand mining racket was busted and 105 tonne sand and equipments worth crores of rupees were seized by the police following a raid on the bank of the river Und in the Jodiya taluka of Jamnagar.

Central Railway officials have sent 11 letters to state authorities in the past four years regarding the rampant dredging between Mumbra and Diva, which is weakening the railway embankment and bridges and the state passes the issue back to railways.
Activists say illegal sand mining rampant in Panvel but no FIR lodged yet.
The Revdanda police team raided the creek at Diwiparangi village in south-east Alibaug on Saturday afternoon and caught five men red-handed while excavating sand and loading them into trucks.

A Right to Information (RTI) activist - Romel Sutharia was allegedly attacked by a group of unidentified persons outside the Collector office in Tapi district of Gujarat for allegedly seeking information and opposing "illegal mining" there. The issue of large-scale illegal mining of sand and stone over Tapi river and across the district was mentioned in Sutharia's complaint.
Mahad effect: WR raises alarm over sand mining near two bridges on the Vaitarna River in Palghar district.

A village in Morbi district of Gujarat witnessed tense scene after sand mafia razed the Dalit locality with an earthmover and loader. Locals allege that the sand miners demolished their homes so that they could make a road through the residential area of the village that would lead directly to the river. However, local police intervened in time to diffuse the brewing situation.
Excessive sand mining in the Kulsi River in Kamrup District of Assam has resulted in the drying up of the river affecting the dolphin population—in one of the main habitats for the dolphin in Assam.
Forest staff of Basugaon range and police bust an illegal sawmill & sand mining and seize two dumpers which smuggled sand minings along the Champawati River in Chirang district, Assam.
Thane district administration cracked down on sand mafia in Kalyan, Dombivli and Bhiwandi.

Fearing crackdown, sand miners move from Ulhas creek to Mumbra.
After mid-day highlighted how the authorities had failed to check rampant dredging at the Diva-Dombivli stretch of Ulhas creek, the sand mafia have vacated the belt and moved operations to the Mumbra area.
42 booked for illegal sand mining along Kalyan creek.

West Bengal Government identified 30 new regions for sand mining , that are to contribute to the added revenue generation in an attempt to support the state government which is facing trouble to run welfare schemes including Lakshmir Bhandar that requires Rs 17,000 crore annually. 30 new sand blocks have been identified and decided to start their mining under the state’s new policy from December in an attempt to generate more revenue.
Under the new sand policy, the state government will not auction sand mines but instead engage agencies to mine sand , and then auction the sand. Considering that the new sand policy would not be implemented on a majority of the sand mines as of now, Bengal chief secretary H. K. Dwivedi asked the district magistrate to find out new sand mines in an attempt to generate more revenue .According to sources, all existing 900 sand mines have been auctioned a few years ago for a period of 5 years.
Kalyan MP asked the Thane Collector to stop illegal sand mining near Mumbra bridge since such activities are making the structure weak.

The Kharkari river, a tributary of the Kulshi river in the Kamrup district of Assam, has faced illegal sand mining which has resulted in starving the crops planted on its banks since water cannot overflow into the fields any longer.
Superintendent of Police killed on a mission to bust sand mining operations in Karbi Anglong in Assam. The mining in the area was controlled by the UPLA.
Revenue department officials along with Sudhagad tehsildar take action against illegal sand dredging and transportation.
Team of local crime branch conducted raids on sand smuggling at Parner and Kopargaon and seized goods worth Rs 47,20,000.

Nayan Kalola, a local farmer cum RTI activist in Vanthali town of Junagadh district in Gujarati was abducted and then brutally beaten up by the sand mafias of the area. They warned him of dire consequences and told him "not to interfere" with the illegal sand mining.
Kalola's is just one story among many in Gujarat who have tangled with the sand mafia. In Gujarat, as in many other parts of the country, two types of illegal sand mining are rampant: illegal mining in the legally leased areas in more than 60 rivers across the state (flouting the rules and taking out more sand than permitted by digging deeper than allowed) and sand mining without permission. The State's Mining and Geology department lays emphasis on increasing drone based surveillance to monitor areas where illegal sand mining takes place.

ED arrested Shantanu Banerjee, Chief Executive of Hooghly Zilla Parishad in recruitment corruption case. After Shantanu's arrest, his large amount of property was traced. In wake of the illegal sand mining activity happening on the 60 kilometres stretch of the “sensitive” Sabarmati riverbed in the districts of Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar and Sabarkantha, Gujarat Government has decided to keep a check by using night vision drones in these areas under the Trinetra Drone Surveillance System. According to then Chief Minister Vijay Rupani -a central command and control room would also be set up for this purpose.

A Navsari based comp M M Infracon continued mining in the tapi river bed near Dumas (Surat) despite its lease agreement expiring in September 2022. As pointed out by The Brackish Water Research Centre(BWRC) - the mining of mud mixed with sand  has caused bank erosion and damaged the river bank and mangroves for nearly a kilometre. BWRC has also written to Gujarat Chief Minister demanding a high-level investigation into this Rs 189 crore sand mining scam.
Ghats of Simhastha Kumbh Mela have become centres of illegal sand mining.
Four fined 3.5 lakh for Illegal sand dredging in Sindhudurg. They were extracting sand beyond the permitted limits at Hadi and Kalaval creek area even though their permission had expired.
Three children drowned in a sand mining pit in Ambawade village in Satara. Villagers allege that illegal sand mining in the river was was the reason the pit was there.

The revenue department seized 70 trucks, 5 earth movers, and 30 boats in Vadoli Bhikeshwar of Karad taluka. The administration also destroyed 52 sand pits that had been excavated on the Krishna river. Satara district is one of the major centres of the sand business in western Maharashtra.
Sand mining destroying natural habitat of crocodiles along the Krishna river in Sangli district.

Illegal sand trade has been reported in Harihar during the lockdown. Villagers in Rajanahalli expressed their anger by stopping a tipper and seizing 10 tippers involved in illegal sand transportation. Congress MLA S. Ramappa accused the police of running the sand racket and demanded action, expressing frustration at the lack of response. Ramappa also highlighted the increasing COVID-19 cases in Harihar taluk and criticized the district administration for inadequate information and control. He warned of a protest in front of the Chief Minister's residence if immediate action is not taken.
The revenue department seized more than 2.7 lakh kg of illegally mined sand from the mafia on the outskirt of Osmanabad city.

A 24-year-old man was killed and his father, a Right to Information activist, was grievously injured after a man accused of illegal sand mining allegedly rammed their scooter with his SUV in Gujarat’s Kutch district. According to the Police Report,RTI activist Ramesh Balia, a native of Meghpar village in Lakhpat tehsil, had lodged complaints of illegal sand mining against Navalsinh Jadeja, who out of grudge rammed his SUV from behind and ran them over.

An aqueduct was built around 2001 for the water from the main narmada canal to flow over the Orsang river. Due to excessive mining around the river, the depth of the river bed has increased exposing the foundation piles of the aqueduct, leading to further damage due to exposure. The Narmada Nigam Authorities had appealed to the District Colllector to further investigate into this matter resulting in the suspension of 11 sand mining leases around Orsang river.

A circle officer and three other revenue officials were allegedly manhandled and threatened by unidentified members of the sand mafia. The officials had intercepted a truck that was carrying illegally mined sand from Daund to Pune. One of them was arrested by the police.
The sand mafia tried to mow down Hingoli tehsildar and his team at Patonda village on Penganga river bank, when they visited the site to stop illegal mining and nab the miners

The intentions and actions of the Andhra Pradesh government to avert illegal sand mining in the Krishna River are questioned by BJP leader Somu Veerraju.

The district administration has identified 190 illegal mining spots across the district since the formation of a special squad for the purpose in July last year, collecting Rs 112.38 lakh in fine from those indulging in unauthorized excavation of sand and minerals at these locations.

Kerala has raised the fine for illegal sand mining from rivers to Rs 5 lakh. It was Rs 25,000 earlier. Governor Arif Mohammed Khan signed the Protection of River Banks and Regulation of Removal of Sand (Amendment) Act that hiked the fine.

The Punjab Cabinet, led by Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi, approved the Punjab State Sand and Gravel Mining Policy, 2021, to make sand and gravel available at affordable rates to the public including sand and gravel loading charges at mining sites. Will go As per the earlier policy, this rate was ₹ 9 cubic feet at the pit head.
Activists and organizations are working towards curbing illegal sand mining in the Kengeri area in Bangalore.

description: Dubiously obtained mining leases, unpaid fines running into crores, fake transit passes and overloaded dumpers are routinely overlooked in a rush to meet Delhi-NCR’s construction needs.

The National Green Tribunal (NGT) rapped the District administration of Balasore over illegal sand mining in Subranarekha riverbed. The tribunal has directed filing of an FIR against former Tehsildar of Basta and penalised an accused of Rs 1 crore.
The locals had alleged that illegal and rampant sand mining in the region has resulted in the depletion of water level, change in the course of the river. Moreover, the approach road constructed inside the river is allegedly obstructing its natural flow.
Besides, the villagers had complained that they are being exposed to air pollution caused by the transportation of excavated sand in open truck.

Revenue officials in Raichur district have discovered a high-tech sand smuggling network misusing permits from other districts. They seized 307 permits worth around 3 lakh rupees. The racket operated in Devadurga taluk, where sand trade was rampant. Three individuals are accused of running the operation through a medical shop. A case has been filed, and efforts are underway to apprehend the culprits.

A 20 year old  and two minors, who were  illegally mining sand were killed while the sand mound caved in and fell off  near the bank of the Balasan river in Siliguri , North Bengal. This incident took place during the morning and the injured bodies were retrieved later , and taken to the hospital.

Farmer Complains to Prime Minister: Abhilakh Singh, a farmer of Bhind district, has complained about the sand mafia to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The sand mafia is trampling the mustard crop. Collector and SP did not take any action on the complaint of the farmer.
This report mentions of  a drone surveillance done by police in Birbhum district in order to assess the illegal sand extraction in regions of Mayurakshi River.

A study conducted by the National Centre for Earth Science Studies (NCESS) has revealed anthropogenic interventions as the main reason for the plight of Munroe Thuruthu residents, Kerala’s first set of climate refugees.
All Assam Adivasi Students Union stages protest against sand mafia operating in the Doikrong river in Numaligarh, Assam.
Trichy city police arrested six people out of the eight booked for indulging in illegal sand mining inThiruverumbur, Kollidam and Kattuputhur areas in Trichy.
Illegal sandmining carried out in the Kapili-kolong, Hel, and Buridihing rivers in Assam using machines, where only manual sandmining is allowed.

Hired software developer Sauvik Chatterjee, arrested for sand smuggling at Bidhannagar cyber crime police . Hasanuzzaman, who was arrested earlier, was interrogated and gave the lead for Souvik. Sand mining has been banned in Uttara Kannada district for eight months, causing a shortage of sand for construction. Allegations of illegal sand extraction and transportation have also emerged, with reports of sand being stolen and sold at high prices to Goa and other places. Recently, an illegal sand transport lorry was caught at the Goa border, leading to demands from the public to curb the illegal trade. Over 100 leaseholders are currently extracting sand from permitted areas, but the closure of mining has led to increased illegal activities. The district administration is being urged to address the sand shortage and take appropriate action to alleviate the problem.
State-owned CIL intends to produce sand using overburden rocks lying at its various coal mines and the operation of five such sand plants is likely to commence by next year, the government said.

The government has proposed to enact a land settlement Act and is considering enabling provisions for legal occupiers of the land to get a conclusive title on ownership. A mobile application would be developed for real-time public reporting of complaints along with photo and geo-tagging about illegal land filling, sand-mining and land encroachment.

The alleged illegal mining of boulders and sand from Anantnag water bodies continues unabated and that too in broad daylight, notwithstanding the inclement weather, right under the nose of the administration.

The Geology and Mining department has busted a racket of illegal sand mining worth Rs. 7.15 crore in Halvad Taluka of Morbi District ( which included Rs. 2.08 crore worth of environmental damage).The department submitted video of drone surveillance, where along with illegally excavated sand, materials like loader machines, excavator machine and four tractors were found.

Officials of the mining department in Punjab’s Mohali district conducted a raid in the Teera village  and recovered a tipper truck and a poclain machine. The department had also nabbed two men mining sand illegally at the spot, according to officials.

The crime branch of Panchkula police has arrested two members of the Bhupi Rana and Davinder Bambiha gangs. Police said they were also involved in illegal sand mining in Panchkula, Ambala and Mohali districts.

An officer from the Mines and Geology Department, Rajesh Tungabhadra, conducted five consecutive days of raids on an illegal sand mining mafia along the riverbanks in Gadag district. Around 750 tippers loaded with sand worth crores were seized during the operations. However, Rajesh has been transferred, raising suspicions of political influence behind the decision. Locals believe the transfer was a result of his refusal to yield to such pressure. The transfer has sparked dissatisfaction in the district. Meanwhile, allegations have been made against a contractor involved in sand mining in Chitradurga district, where sand is being illegally extracted beyond permissible depths. The illegal activities are causing the Vedavati riverbanks to drain, impacting groundwater levels and drying up farmers' borewells. Farmers are demanding that authorities take action to curb the illegal sand trade and prevent further environmental damage.

Mining of minerals and runoff of various pesticides are taking a heavy toll on different species of fingerlings (Guran) in Romeshi stream, a vital tributary of Jhelum flowing through Pulwama. Residents informed Rising Kashmir that discharge of pesticides and extraction of boulders and sand from Romeshi pose a threat to many fingerling species.
Both Legal and illegal sandmining has resulted in water draining from the Chandubi Lake (a hotspot for flora and fauna) into the deepening Kulsi river, affecting the wildlife of the region.

A team of revenue officials led by Kalyan and Dombivli tahsildar carried out a raid at Thane creek and found two barges using suction pumps for dredging sand crush. The suction pumps were seized and destroyed using gas cutters, while sugar was poured into the engines of both the barges, disabling them.
This report discusses the overall crisis faced due to sand mining in Indian states .

Former chief minister Uma Bharti who has been taking the government to task over the sale of liquor has ripped into the government for illegal mining. She tweeted that when she was coming from Delhi to Morena, she saw hundreds of sand-laden tractor-trolleys under the Chambal bridge.

Four labourers were killed when an embankment collapsed on them near the bank of the Goma river in Gujarat’s Vadodara district late on Thursday, PTI reported. They were allegedly loading illegally mined sand when the embankment gave way, a police official said.
E-auctioning to be introduced for sand extraction in Assam via the AMTRON portal to combat the rampant corruption, malpractices present in the sector, and to increase transparency in the process.

The Bengal government has reignited the mining of minor minerals — sand, pebbles and stones — from riverbeds of the state from October 8.For the past few months, extraction of such items from riverbeds had stopped following instructions of the National Green Tribunal. In July this year, the Mamata Banerjee cabinet came up with a new policy that centralised the auction system for mining such items.The order has come as a relief for lakhs of workers, who load and unload these basic construction items, and thousands of truck drivers and owners.

Critics approach Kottayam Collector with a request to stop the works immediately saying that works will hamper the natural elevation of the river bed and destroy the riparian eco-system. Irrigation dept. maintains that the work does not include deepening of the river bed but removal of silt deposit.

Order of the National Green Tribunal in the matter of Residents of Bhatpara Municipality Vs State of West Bengal dated 14/10/2019 regarding illegal sand mining in District North 24 Parganas, West Bengal, near Naihati Bandel Railway Bridge, Kanchrapara Bansberia Road Bridge at Jagatdal Meghna Ghat.


Report submitted by the State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) and the letter of District Magistrate affirmed the presence of illegal mining and its closure but further time was requested to recover environmental compensation.

Members of the Rapid Response Cell (Rajkot Range) were carrying out routine supervision at Bhatia outpost when they came across an unusual activity. Suspecting it to be illegal sand mining, they raided the place that is owned by Dadubhai Kambariya. Cops seized stock of illegally mined sand and other equipment as well as vehicles(worth Rs. 14.45 crores). It is suspected by the opposition party that local politicians and police were hand in glove with those carrying out illegal sand mining activities.

Bapi Naskar, one of the kingpins of the sand smuggling ring in Sonarpur, has now been caught by the police. With this, the number of people arrested in the sand theft business has increased to 4. However, many of the main accused are still absconding. 

সোনারপুরের (Sonarpur) খেয়াদায় বালি পাচার চক্রের পাণ্ডাদের অন্যতম বাপি নস্কর এবার পুলিশের (Police) জালে। এই নিয়ে বালি-চুরির কারবারে ধৃতের সংখ্যা বেড়ে হল ৪। তবে মূল অভিযুক্তদের অনেকেই এখনও পলাতক।

दिसंबर 2020 से मार्च 2022 तक यानी 16 महीनों में रेत खनन की वजह से देशभर में कम से कम 418 लोगों की जान गई है और 438 लोग घायल हुए हैं। इनमें 49 मौत खनन के लिए नदियों में बनाए गए कुंड में डूबने से हुई हैं। खनन के चलते सड़क हादसों या डूबने से होने वाली मौत का अलग से कोई सरकारी लेखा-जोखा नहीं है। नदी से कितना खनन किया गया? तय मात्रा से अधिक उपखनिज तो नहीं निकाला गया? इन सब पर निगरानी रखने की कोई व्यवस्था नहीं है। खनन की मात्रा का आकलन करने के लिए बेहतर तरीका ईजाद करने में जुटे वैज्ञानिक मानते हैं कि आमतौर पर तय सीमा से अधिक खनन किया जाता है। पर्यावरण कार्यकर्ता खनन से जुड़े मामलों में केंद्र या राज्य सरकार की तरफ से की जाने वाली कार्रवाइयों में पारदर्शिता लाने की मांग कर रहे हैं। उनका मानना है कि खनन से जुड़े मामलों में सरकार की तरफ से मजबूत इच्छाशक्ति नहीं दिखाई देती।

Non-stop sand mining, development projects near rivers, deforestation in the catchment areas and unplanned dams are killing the major rivers of Madhya Pradesh. The state is now facing an acute deficit of water. Tapti and Shipra have almost died while the Narmada river is also facing dry spells.

Mukesh Darbar of Jetalpur (Ahmedabad) had informed the Mines and Minerals Department about the illegal sand mining taking place in Narol. He was beaten up by Kuldeep Singh Parmar and his brothers for lodging the complaint, the three accused then allegedly threatened him, saying that if he ever informed the officials about their sand mining, they would kill him.
4 shot dead in gang war over illegal sand mining in rural Patna
A 10-year-old boy drowned after slipping into a pit on Leesh river bed in West Bengal's Jalpaiguri, suspected to have been dug for illegal sand mining purposes.

Betaj Badsha Anuvrata Mondal of Birbhum has already been arrested by the CBI in the case of cow smuggling. Along with cow smuggling, strong investigation is going on with coal smuggling. After cow-coal, now illegal stone-sand smuggling is under the ED's eye. Meanwhile, cases of sand and stone smuggling have started to pile up. The Enforcement Directorate has launched a separate investigation in this matter.

Asansol Durgapur Police Commissionerate is working to stop illegal sand smuggling. In such a case, the Niamatpur outpost police of Kulti police station conducted a raid and seized three tractors and a dumper loaded with sand from Niamatpur area. After this, the sand-laden vehicles were handed over to the BLLR and officials. On the other hand, according to sand traders, the police have unnecessarily seized our vehicles even though these sand-laden vehicles have valid documents.
The Water Resources Department has initiated the process of opening new quarries in the Cauvery and the Kollidam in Tiruchi and Karur districts.
Six men were arrested and several vehicles engaged in illegal sand mining were impounded from the river beds in Himachal Pradesh's Una district.

The dispute between the Odisha and West Bengal governments over sand mining on the Subarnarekha riverbed finally has been solved after officials from Balasore and Paschim Medinipur districts in the neighbouring state reached the spot and conducted an inquiry.
Seven men attacked a six member team of the Geology and Minin Department when they went to investigate the illegal sand mining at Hirapur village in Ahmedabad.

The state government has decided to extend the environment clearance (EC) obtained by earlier lessees of 88 mining leases for two years, so that those who win the auction can start mining activities immediately.

Three teenagers decided to take a dip in the village pond of Shikarpur of the Bhachau taluka. However, while bathing those three drowned as the depth of the pond was increased due to excessive sand mining in the region.

Senior Gujarat-based environmentalists Rohit Prajapati and of the Krishnakant of the Paryavaran Suraksha Samiti (PSS) in a letter to the Union secretary, Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change, have said that “illegal” sand mining in Bhavnagar, coastal district, is “contaminating and degrading the ground water, rivers, lakes, other water resources and check dams.

description: Meena is among hundreds of victims of attacks by the mining mafia in Rajasthan, a state where such incidents are on the rise. Others include anti-mining activists, locals, journalists, bureaucrats and even police officials. A majority of these attacks are carried out by gangs involved in the mining of riverbed sand, which is in fact at the heart of illegal mining practices in the state. The article further talks about the relentless mining on the khatedari lands. This is the first instalment in a series on illegal mining in Rajasthan.

Forest department ranger of Upper Assam arrested for largescale anomalies in operation of the Daigrung river sand quarry in Golaghat district. It is alleged that they issued depot stock challans and transit passes for illegal operation of the sand quarry.

The mining department is introducing a special security paper to rule out forgery and duplicity of royalty. The special paper will be issued to all the leaseholders in the state and will have digital watermarking, embossed hologram, unique identification mark among other features, officials said.

MP Prajwal Revanna, during a District Development Co-ordination and Monitoring Committee (DISHA) meeting at the Hassan Zilla Panchayat Hall, expressed his concerns about illegal sand mining in Sakaleshpur. He criticized the officials for turning a blind eye to the issue and accused them of being involved in bribery. Prajwal alleged that those involved in sand peddling were supported by the police and earned around Rs 40,000 per lorry per month. He boldly confronted the Superintendent of Police, stating that he had noticed instances of bribes being taken. Prajwal's unique style of speaking sets him apart from other leaders, as he addresses issues directly and without monotony.

In the past four years, SAS Nagar district mining department got 21 FIRs registered and recovered Rs 3.97 crore as fine. Mining department officials said that action will be taken against the violators in the coming days. Executive engineer said that they have recovered Rs 27.50 lakh as penalty from vehicles involved in transporting the sand and gravel illegally. Additionally, Rs 3.70 crore in fines was recovered from the material, which was illegally transported into the state.

The District Collector of Dakshina Kannada, MR Ravikumar, has granted permission for traditional sand mining in the district. This approval allows sand mining in the Netravati River and Phalguni River under the Coastal Regulation Zone (CTZ), with the condition that it must be carried out manually without the use of machines. The decision was made following a meeting with a 7-member committee from the Mines and Geology Department. Around 202 individuals have been authorized to conduct sand mining, and official sand supply is expected to commence in the coming week. The district administration received 282 applications for the tender process, and after careful evaluation, 202 applications were approved for sand dune clearing.

Illegal sand mining is rampant in the rural areas of Koppal district, with the police confiscating around ten trucks daily. However, vehicle owners often release their impounded trucks through the courts, making it challenging to curb the illegal trade. To tackle this issue, District SP Arunangshu Giri has devised a new strategy. He has instructed the Revenue Department and Mines Geology Department to identify approved sandblasting points and survey lands where unauthorized mining is taking place. If illegal points are discovered, the land will be seized, and cases will be filed against the landowners. This collaborative approach aims to deter illegal sand mining by targeting both the mining sites and the owners. With over 300 illegally transporting sand seized under SP Giri's tenure, the joint efforts of the police, revenue, and mining geology departments hope to successfully control the illegal sand mining trade in the district.

district: Vadodara, Surat, Rajkot, Ahmadabad, Sabar Kantha
description: During this five year period(2015-2020) a total of 38,117 cases of illegal mining were registered across different districts of Gujarat.Out of the 38,117 odd cases of illegal mining registered, First Information Reports (FIRs) were filed against suspects in only 2.16 percent of the cases.When asked about the low percentage of FIRs lodged in illegal mining cases, DM Shukla, Additional Director, Commissioner of Geology and Mining (CGM), said in a statement mailed to The Indian Express, “When cases of illegal mining is found, government issues a notice for penalty. If the accused is ready to pay penalty, the government recovers the compounding fee from the accused person… If the accused is not ready to pay the penalty, then the government lodges an FIR.”

As houses continue to crumble in the ‘sinking’ Himalayan town of Joshimath, activists and environmentalists have warned of similar situations in other parts of India. Some cite activities such as sand mining as a lead-up to land subsidence. Meanwhile, alarm bells are already ringing in West Bengal's Darjeeling as houses develop cracks

The South Goa Sand Transporters have urged the government to take steps to immediately re-start legal sand mining so that they can resume the operations and eke a living on the activity. A delegation of the Association will also called on the Chief Minister Pramod Sawant with a plea to grant permission for the legal sand mining as per the rules in force.
The police have booked two persons, including a sarpanch, for allegedly entering into a scuffle and stopping a government employee from discharging his duties.

Unwarranted sand mining is adding to the plight of the Nonai River in Udalguri district. The villagers are having sleepless nights due to rampant sand mining in Nonai, as the river has been changing its course and moving toward the inhabited areas—eroding their lands.

Six journalists were booked in Madhya Pradesh’s Khargone district on July 2 for alleged rioting and abusing on the complaint of District Mining Officer (DMO), according to the police. Reportedly, the journalists had gone to meet the DMO on the same evening seeking his comment on the issue of rampant illegal mining and storage of sand in the district.

Illegal sand collection has been rampant along the Tungabhadra river in Mundaragi taluk, Gadag district. Sand mafia have been using rafts to loot sand from the shallow waters, particularly around Hammigi village. Despite there being enough water in the river, villagers are puzzled as to where the sand is coming from. The demand for this rich sand is high in nearby areas such as Gadag, Hubli, and Dharwad. The illegal traders employ a method where sand is removed from the water using a bamboo stick attached to a bag. Lack of coordination between mining, revenue, and police departments has allowed the illegal sand trade to continue. The local residents accuse the Tehsildar and CPI officers of turning a blind eye to the activities. The Mines Department officials plan to communicate with the Tehsildar and CPI to address the issue.
Protests against illegal mining in the Manah river in the Bongaigaon district of Assam. Illegal mining had resulted in rampant erosion compelling locals into protest.
Gauhati HC seeks officer's report on alleged illegal sand mining in the Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC) of Assam.

Shradha Pandre, the sub-divisional forest officer (Chambal Sanctuary), who has been attacked earlier as well, accused police officers of supporting the illegal mining mafia. She added they are not letting her curb the illegal sand mining menace

Illegal silt mining in the Brahmaputra riverbed has turned out to be a threat to Auckland and its nearby area in Dibrugarh. The sources informed at each day at least 50 dumpers extract silt from the Brahmaputra.

The death of a 10 year old by sand truck in Dhubri district triggered violence in the Bilashipara area in which the angered locals burnt down three sand laden trucks, a gravel storage site, apart from blocking the road.
Police officials were caught on camera while giving free pass to illegal sand traders working in the district by accepting bribes from truck drivers in Assam's Karbi Anglong.
A herd of over 50 goats were killed while 30 others were injured after a sand-laden truck in Nayagarh district of Odisha ran over them.

The Karnataka Lokayukta police conducted raids in Dakshina Kannada district, seizing assets worth Rs 40 lakh, including vehicles, in connection with alleged illegal sand mining. After receiving multiple complaints, Lokayukta SP K Laxmi Ganesh formed three teams to investigate the matter. The raids took place in Belthangady, Bantwal, and Mulky, resulting in the confiscation of earthmovers, tippers, and other assets. The seized items were handed over to the respective police stations, and three criminal cases have been registered. The Lokayukta received 25 complaints from the public regarding illegal sand mining. Laxmi Ganesh mentioned that complaints were also filed against the revenue department, pollution control board, and Mangaluru Urban Development Authority, and appropriate action will be taken against them.

Illegal sand mining along the banks of river Pahumara in Lower Assam’s Bajali district, has posed a serious threat to the people residing in Rajakhat area. Extensive sand mining along the river banks have threatened the livelihood of the people in the area, in the past few years, floods have destroyed houses, livestock and farmlands.

Illegall sand mining on the banks of the Beki river in Barpeta district of Assam create havoc among the locals. The area being prone to floods and erosion, illegal sand mining has aggravated the problem. Despite resistance from the locals, the sand mafias still continue mining.

Sub-inspector (SI) was placed under suspension for dereliction of duty after the death of a sand mining ghat lessee at Manei in Kharasrota river in bomb attack. Jajpur SP Rahul PR suspended SI of Binjharpur police station Kanduri Charan Das for failing to take any action on the FIR lodged by the victim Surendra Dash.
Three children were buried alive after a mound of mud caved in at Koiritola in Sharda village in Jharkhand’s Garhwa district

Water Resources Department has opened two sand quarries on Cauvery riverbed in Karur district. The opening of quarries has received strong reaction among environmentalists and activists of Cauvery Protection Movement. They claim that the authorities had erred by opening quarries. An advocate Commissioner appointed by the High Court had visited the sites in 2017 and reported that sand had been extracted extensively by violating conditions. It was after the visit of the advocate Commissioner that the sand quarries in the Cauvery and the Kollidam were closed in 2018. The authorities should not have opted for opening the quarries at the same locations. It would worsen the impact of overexploitation of sand in the river and its banks, they maintained.

The conclave of North Geology and Mining Ministers resolved to request the Ministry of Mines to revive its funding under National Mineral Exploration Trust (NMET) to include minor minerals exploration at least for the North-Eastern States. This funding, which was stopped, would help in the process of exploration and carrying out due processes outlined in the sand mining guidelines 2020.

A Trinamool Congress leader was shot dead in broad daylight at Ketugram in West Bengal's East Burdwan district. Local BJP leaders have claimed that the event was the fallout of infighting in the ruling party over illegal sand mining in the area.
The SDM had narrow escape when the sand mafia tried to mow him down under the truck during a raid.
Inter-state (Jharkhand-Uttar Pradesh) sand mafia racket is still active in Garhwa district which witnessed a major sand mining violence episode in May 2017 resulting in 5 deaths.

The Karnataka government has proposed the establishment of a dedicated protection force to combat illegal sand mining in the state, according to the Department of Mines and Geology's submission to the National Green Tribunal (NGT). The government has already empowered the police, revenue, Public Works Department (PWD), and Forest Department to take action against illegal mining activities. The government has blocked unauthorized village roads leading to water bodies and identified sand blocks for scientific and sustainable mining through auctions. The state emphasizes the importance of desilting ponds, lakes, tanks, and streams to maintain their existence and prevent water collection issues. To monitor transportation, vehicles of lessees are equipped with GPS, and weigh bridges and CCTVs have been installed at key locations to prevent illegal activities.

description:
This report highlights the issue of sand mafias and illegal sand mining in India, focusing on various states such as Karnataka, NCR, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan. The report describes how these sand mafias operate as a network of influential politicians, construction companies, and miners, breaching regulations and exploiting the demand for sand in the construction industry. It mentions instances where complaints by locals about illegal sand mining were ignored, indicating the power and violence of the criminal network.

The report emphasizes that the activities of sand mafias lead to environmental degradation, including river erosion and alteration of river courses. It also points out the lax enforcement of regulations, with miners and builders bypassing licensing requirements and evading the payment of royalties. The profitability of illegal sand mining is highlighted, with low investments and high returns.

Furthermore, the report mentions the risks faced by those who oppose the sand mafias, citing cases of violence and even deaths of individuals who exposed their operations. It discusses the jurisdictional issues surrounding sand mining and the need for stricter implementation of laws and regulations.

Overall, the report presents an analysis of the scale and impact of sand mafias and illegal sand mining in India, shedding light on the systemic challenges, environmental consequences, and the need for stronger government action and civil society engagement to address this issue.

Compiled with data from various government departments and the National Institute of Oceanography (NIO), the report underscores the urgent need for intervention to address cumulative impacts on the riverine and estuarine ecosystems.

The National Green Tribunal (NGT) Principal Bench in Delhi has mandated Maharashtra to adhere strictly to the Sustainable Sand Mining Management Guidelines of 2016, set by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) in the Akola illegal

mining case where 58 sand ghats were auctioned without preparing district survey repot (DSR)

The NGT highlighted the need for robust monitoring at all stages of mining to maintain river ecology. It condemned the Akola authorities for fabricating a DSR and allowed the petitioner to seek further action from the MoEFCC's high-powered committee. Additionally, the NGT directed the implementation of strict measures such as demarcating mining areas, using CCTV, GPS tracking, and establishing a call center to ensure transparency and compliance in sand mining operations.

Rampant mechanised sand mining going on in the Bargarh district, especially at night. The sand is then sold elsewhere outside of the district at higher prices. Hoarding of sand is also done to sell at premium rates during the monsoon season when there is a shortfall due to ban. Royalty is not being properly collected for such huge mining by the affected areas of Maneswar and Bheden tehsil. Huge craters have formed on the riverbed affecting the riparian communities.

A petition was filed by local residents for widespread degradation of the Mahanadi river bed due to unchecked sand mining operations at Nuapatana under Tangi-Choudwar tehsil in Cuttack district. NGT’s East Zone Bench imposed environmental compensation of  Rs. 38.28 lakh to be paid within three months' time. It also directed authorities concerned to ensure sand mining on river Mahanadi to be done as per the provisions and guidelines of Sustainable Sand Mining Management Guidelines 2016 and Enforcement and Monitoring Guidelines for Sand Mining 2020. The NGT bench also mentioned that a future study might be carried out on annual natural replenishment of sand in that area.

An assistant sub-inspector (ASI) was crushed to death by a tractor-trolley carrying illegally mined sand in Shahdol, Madhya Pradesh, on Saturday night. When police tried to stop the sand-laden tractor, the driver crushed the assistant inspector of police and fled, leaving the tractor out of control.

September 2021:


- Odisha's State Sand Mining Policy was to be rolled out by the Revenue and Disaster Management department soon.

- The Revenue department in consultation with the Water Resources and Odisha Space Application Centre (ORSAC) will identify potential sand sources suitable for mining and conduct survey of them for improved location accuracy.

- IITs and other institutions will be taken into consultation for understanding the river-bed geomorphology keeping sustainability in mind.

- A surveillance system for the source extraction will also be incorporated.

- Mechanised mining would be prohibited through the policy.

- DSRs and gap assessments will be made to bridge the demand-supply through sustainable efforts.

- The policy bans quarrying sand through mechanised suction method and blasting.

- Besides, no mining operation will be allowed in safety zones as well as prohibitory areas prescribed under Odisha Minor MineralConcession Rules - 2016.

The Nagpur bench of Bombay high court has initiated suo motu cognizance regarding the unauthorized excavation of murrum and cutting down of trees in the eco-sensitive zone (ESZ) of Katepurna Wildlife Sanctuary in Akola district

Even with police seizing multiple machineries and imposing fines for sand mining in the district of Jagatsinghapur, particularly in the Mahanadi riverbed, illegal sand extraction in heaps of quantities could not be stopped. Illegal activities of sand mafia in the area has been on the rise. Severe soil erosion of several villages on the bankside under Tirtol, Raghunathpur and Kujang tehsils on downstream River Mahanadi is threatening the local communities.

Illegal sand mining activities is thriving in Wainganga River in Bhandara District since June, following the end of the auction period. This activity, overlooked by authorities, has caused significant revenue losses and supports Nagpur's construction market. The sand mafias are involved for years and operate without fear.

Illegal sand mining reached a brisk rate in Allipingal, Tarapur, Jaipur, Tirtol and Naugaon of Jagatsinghpur district right before the monsoons. In one of the indicidents, the sand traders had encroached Mahanadi river bank in Tirtol to stock huge quantity of sand without taking permission from the local Tehsildar. 


The traders, who had stocked the sand, sold it for `1000 to `1200 per tractor instead of normal rate of `600. Traders are stocking it up to sell during the monsoon season at double the usual rate. Some have also forcibly occupied hundreds of acres of land of the farmers to stock the sand. Contractors are also violating the norms by allowing traders to export sand outside the district. Amongst all of this, unauthorised sand quarrying has led to severe erosion of river banks in Tirtol, Raghunathpur and Kujang situated in Mahanadi downstream. Amidst several agitations made by the villagers till date, no preventive step has been taken so far.

In a letter addressed to the district collector, VKMC highlighted that the Maharashtra government has introduced a new sand policy this year to curb illegal sand mining and ensure that sand is available to the public at a fair cost.

Madhya Pradesh high court has sought to know from state govt what steps are being taken to prevent illegal sand mining and killing of govt employees. A police officer and a patwari have been killed by the sand mafia in Shahdol district in the last six months.

The NGT has formed a joint committee to look into the complaints of illegal mining in Yamuna Khadar area of Kairana region in Shamli district. The joint committee will be tasked with visiting the site, conducting a probe, and submit submitting an action report. To the tribunal within two months.


The committee includes the member secretary of CPCB a representative of the UPPCB regional officer of the Ministry of environment Forest and climate change and Shamli district magistrate


The complainant has raised multiple issues about violations of environmental conditions and destruction of the river.

The 400 sq km Painganga Wildlife Sanctuary spread in Yavatmal and Nanded districts is facing severe threat from politically backed sand mafia. On Sunday (November 2015), the sand mafia tried to run over three revenue department talathis who attempted to stop them fleeing from Umarkhed. The spot from where sand was excavated is 7km away from the sanctuary, which falls in the eco-sensitive zone (ESZ).


There are multiple instances of mining activity, confrontation by forest department staff and special task forces, and collusion by some forest dept staff mentioned in the article as well.

In perhaps one of the biggest illegal mining scams in the country, at Pachgaon near Nagpur, at least 21 forest officials and employees may face action if the list submitted to the Nagpur bench of Bombay High Court is considered. The court had asked the forest department to submit names of officers and staff who neglected or ignored excavation in forest land abutting survey numbers 255 and 256 when they were supposed to oversee the said area.

The deputy conservator of forest (DyCF) submitted a list of 21 employees who were posted in Nagpur division from January 1, 2001 to November 1, 2013, the period when mining on forest land and encroachments was rampant in Pachgaon.

The Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal (NGT) in Delhi has accepted a petition that challenges the auctioning of 58 sand ghats in Akola district. This auction was conducted without adhering to the guidelines set by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) for environmental clearance.


in March, 34 sand ghats were e-auctioned for a royalty of Rs4.85 crore without district survey report (DSR), which is an important initial step before permitting sand mining and granting environment clearance (EC). However, permits to extract sand through e-auction were granted on March 5, without preparing the mandatory DSR.

The Akola district collectorate’s decision to auction 34 sand ghats without a mandatory district survey report (DSR) has come in for a sharp criticism from local wildlife lovers and environmentalists. In March, a total of 34 sand ghats out of 45 were electronically auctioned for a royalty of Rs4.85 crore without the DSR, which is a crucial prerequisite for allowing sand mining and obtaining environmental clearance.

description: Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) has started conducting public hearing regarding auctioning of sand ghats across Vidarbha on digital platforms. According to experts, such hearings are not just against the norms but also deprive participation of crucial stakeholders.

A number of villages surrounding the Mahanadri river in the districts of Cuttack and Kendrapara are in a compounding fear due to the floodplain eroding fast from the weak embankments and continually increasing effects from sand mining which has aggravated the process of erosion leading to washing away of many trees around the banks. Excess sand lifting has resulted in changing the course of the river where floodwaters are not uncommon and this has destroying the natural floodplain by eroding almost 200 feet of the area. Villagers claim that the sand mafia keep operating without any fear by getting direct or indirect help from local political leaders and revenue officials, even though their five-year-term lease agreements have lapsed.

Over 340 activists from the Cauvery Protection Movement, including CPI leader R. Nallakannu, were arrested in Karur while protesting illegal sand mining on the Cauvery riverbed. The activists, who handed video evidence of the illegal activities to the district administration, demanded the closure of the sand mines. Coordinator Mukilan highlighted that illegal mining was rampant along a 3-km stretch of the river. During a peaceful rally, protesters were detained by police after being stopped in Thalava Palayam. Nallakannu accused the illegal operations of using 15 earthmovers instead of the permitted two, negatively impacting the groundwater and causing significant financial losses to the state. Human rights NGO People's Watch called for the release of the detained activists, emphasizing their constitutional right to protest.

In a major crackdown on illegal mining, the forest department seized over 800 vehicles and recovered Rs 3.46 crore in fines during the 2017-18 financial year in the western circle. Conservator of Forests Parag Madhukar Dhakate noted a rise in illegal mining, prompting consistent action by the department and Special Task Force. Significant operations were conducted in areas like Terai east, Ramnagar, and Haldwani forest divisions, notably reducing illegal activities on riverbeds such as Gaula, Kosi, Dabka, Nandhaur, and Sharada. The department plans to continue its stringent measures against illegal mining.

The National Green Tribunal (NGT) has requested a detailed list of individuals allegedly involved in illegal mining along the Betwa River in Uttar Pradesh's Jalaun and Hamirpur districts. NGT Chairperson Justice Swatanter Kumar instructed the district magistrates to submit this list by September 27, 2016.

The National Environment Care Federation (NECF), an NGO, released a document featuring sting video footage that exposes illegal sand mining in coastal and riverbed areas in the undivided Dakshina Kannada district. Shashidhar Shetty, the convener of NECF, emphasized that sand mining in coastal Karnataka is a multi-crore scam worth over Rs. 850 crore annually. He revealed that it took more than two years to gather the necessary documents proving the illegal activities, including a year-long sting operation conducted in Udupi and Dakshina Kannada districts. 


Shetty explained that while only fishing communities are legally permitted to mine sand using traditional boats with proper licenses, the sting operation uncovered the use of mechanical equipment and illegal extraction beyond the permissible limits. The mining was also found to be occurring near bridges on National Highways. Furthermore, he noted that licenses have been granted to mine sand even within the Coastal Regulation Zones (CRZ). Shetty mentioned that a petition challenging the legality of mining in these zones has already been filed and is currently under review by the National Green Tribunal (NGT) in New Delhi. He also pointed out that the mining activities have severely damaged mangrove islands, and the duration of the ban on mining has been reduced without scientific justification. The video evidence has been forwarded to all relevant authorities for further investigation.

The henchmen of sand mafia attacked Banka SDPO Dinesh Chandra Srivastava, who was leading a police team and mining department officials at Jathore ghat near Janakpur village under Amarpur police station in Banka district on Tuesday night. A truck driver was killed in the firing by those involved in illegal sand mining. The deceased was identified as Fantoosh Yadav.


Earlier on Tuesday afternoon, the police and mining department team had raided the sand ghats at Rajoun in Banka district and seized several trucks and 11 tractors laden with sand.

Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) persists in conducting public hearings on the digital platform for the auctioning of sand ghats in the region, despite facing significant opposition from environmentalists.

After the clash with the sand mafia and mining officials on Monday over illegal sand excavation, Mining Officer Maheshwar Paswan has filed an application in Banka police station to register an FIR against 41 named people as well as 55 unknown people.


The incident happened when a raid was conducted in Chandan river near Lakhnouri village of Banka police station area. Illegal mining of sand was taking place in Chandan River by cutting the embankment built for flood protection near Lakhnauri village. Sand was being loaded on 15-20 tractors. The people on the mining site attempted to run away on seeing the oficers, and then about 60-65 people returned armed with weapons and attacked.


It was estimated hat 9 lakh 60 thousand cubic feet of sand had been stolen whose mineral value is Rs 3 crore 36 lakh. After imposing the fine, a total of Rs 3 crore 56 lakh 47 thousand 600 had to be paid.
