description: To tackle the shortage of natural river sand and reduce illegal mining, the Maharashtra government has launched a new policy promoting the use of artificial sand (M-sand) in construction. The policy mandates 20% M-sand use in government projects initially, aiming for 100% within three years. It encourages setting up 50–60 M-sand units per district, offering incentives like concessional royalty rates, MSME benefits, power charge exemptions, and stamp duty waivers. A centralized e-auction system will be introduced to ensure transparency. The move aims to ensure a sustainable construction material supply while protecting the environment.

ETV Bharat reports that an illegal sand miner was arrested in Raisen, Madhya Pradesh, for carrying out unauthorized mining in the Narmada riverbed and threatening villagers at gunpoint. Police seized vehicles and equipment from the site and have launched a further investigation.

Madhya Pradesh could become the first government to auction four major reservoirs (Bargi Dam, Tawa Dam, Indira Sagar Dam and Bansagar) for sand mining. Officials have said that the sand mining will be done using machines by contractors with experience. Having received bountiful rain, the government has stated that it has calculated the amount of sand that can be mined and will keep the base price accordingly for auctioning. 


(River names are not mentioned in the report, but picked up and added as tags from names of dams mentioned.)

Despite a statewide ban on mechanised sand mining imposed by the Chief Minister, illegal mining continues unabated in the Ken River, particularly in Chhatarpur and Panna districts of Madhya Pradesh. Villagers from Hinota and Baghari villages, led by sarpanches Sunita Singh and Jhallu Singh, have been protesting for over a week and plan to launch a Jal Satyagraha.

Villagers reported that heavy earthmoving machines and trucks were actively operating, with sand mafia intimidating locals and violating mining rules. Trucks overloaded with sand were allegedly parked 12 km from the site, obtaining pit passes after loading, violating norms.


Though the district collector denied mechanised mining, villagers submitted formal complaints, citing air pollution and health issues. The mining contract is held by a Jabalpur-based firm, but operations are reportedly controlled by parties from Uttar Pradesh, with sand transported to cities like Lucknow, Kanpur, and Raebareli.
The report mentions that illegal sand mining on River Ken is a big menace in the Chattarpur district of Madhya Pradesh. It mentions that official contracts were given only for a few mines.

Social activist Medha Patkar has approached the National Green Tribunal  alleging rampant illegal sand mining in the catchment and submergence areas of the Sardar Sarovar Project across four Madhya Pradesh districts—Barwani, Dhar, Alirajpur, and Khargone. She also reported that Narmada Bachao Andolan volunteers and NAPM’s national convener are facing threats from the sand mafia in Barwani.

Responding to the plea, the NGT Central Zonal Bench, Bhopal (Justice Dalip Singh and expert member A.R. Yousuf) directed the state government to submit:

1. Royalty collection records post expiry of environmental clearances from MPPCB or SEIAA

2. Details of preventive measures, seizures, FIRs, penalties, and illegal sand transport enforcement across all four districts


The case, originally filed in February 2014 before the Jabalpur Bench of the Madhya Pradesh High Court, was transferred to the NGT.

Sub-Divisional Magistrate  (SDM) Ajaygarh in Panna district alleges a local Congress leader of interference by freeing a confiscated sand-laden truck linked to illegal sand mining operations which belonged to him. She also writes that a police officer misbehaved and did not follow her orders. Cases have been registered under under Sections 353 (assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of duty) and 186 (obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions). She regularly monitors sand mining activities and carries out confiscations of trucks. She and her team had she demolished a temporary (and illegal) 20-metre-long bridge built by the mafia to facilitate the mining and transportation of sand in March. The sand mining operations have been a political and environmental issue between the Congress and BJP.

नर्मदापुरम स्थित जवाली रेत खदान पर रेत ठेका कर्मचारी और ग्रामीणों के बीच विवाद हो गया. विवाद इतना बड़ा कि ग्रामीणों ने ठेका कर्मचारियों और उनके वाहनों पर पथराव कर दिया. हमले में करीब 6 गाड़ियों के शीशे टूट गए. जबकि दो कर्मचारी घायल हो गए. आरोप है कि ग्रामीण मजदूरी नहीं मिलने पर रेत खदान को बंद करने की जिद पर अड़े थे. जिसके बाद उन्होंने पथराव कर दिया.

The article highlights the rampant illegal sand mining along the Narmada River in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, which is causing severe ecological damage and revenue loss. Despite only eight authorised mining sites, illegal operations thrive with the tacit support of the government. Over 1,000 unregistered dumpers operate nightly, transporting sand worth thousands of rupees per trip, yet government coffers remain empty.


The sand mafia, allegedly backed by politicians and local dons, operates with impunity, even during banned rainy seasons. This unchecked mining has led to droughts, reduced water levels in the Bargi Dam, and sections of the Narmada drying up. The article warns that without urgent intervention, the Narmada could face extinction, akin to the Saraswati River. It calls for civil society and environmentalists to act before irreversible harm is done.

An assistant sub-inspector (ASI) has been crushed to death by a tractor-trolley used for transporting illegally mined sand in Madhya Pradesh’s Shahdol district. The article describes death due to the practice of "piloting" via which a vehicle moves ahead of a truck used for sand mining to ensure no police intervention. In this case, there was an ASI that was attempting to stop the vehicle, but the tractor-trolley mowed him, resulting in his death. Two persons have been arrested in connection with the incident which took place on the intervening night of Saturday-Sunday in Badoli village.

In Ambah, Morena district of Madhya Pradesh, forest officials were attempting to curb illegal sand mining activities were confronted by villagers. While the officials were securing a tractor-trolley filled with sand from the Chambal River, a group of nine individuals arrived on motorcycles, threatened the officials, and forcibly took back the seized tractor. The forest team documented the incident with photos and videos and filed a complaint with the Ambah police. Authorities are investigating the matter using the recorded evidence to identify and take action against the perpetrators.

In Umaria district, Baba Mahakal Minerals (sand contract company) is allegedly involved in widespread illegal sand mining with the connivance of the local administration and Mineral Department. Despite having no approved leases or demarcated sites, the company is reportedly extracting sand from unapproved areas using large machines during the night hours (7pm to 7am). After a writ petition was filed, the High Court petition has demanded an investigation.


Social worker Ayodhya Prasad Prajapati, who filed the petition, claims he has received death threats from company employees. The company is also accused of fraudulently using transport permits (TPs) from other regions and violating mining regulations, including the NGT’s rules. Additionally, armed outsiders linked to the company are allegedly operating illegally at sand testing posts, creating fear in surrounding villages. A company employee, Gurulal Singh, is reported to be extorting money from tractor drivers under the guise of issuing TP tokens without any legal documentation.

A major action was taken against illegal sand mining in Betul, Madhya Pradesh. Under this, the ADM court has imposed a penalty of Rs 37 crores. This action has been taken in four cases of illegal sand mining. Apart from this, instructions have also been given to confiscate 2 Poklands and a JCB worth Rs 1.25 crore. This was based on action taken by collector and district magistrate on the night 14th and 15th May 2024 and different amount of mined sand was confiscated along with JCBs were  on 7 miners living across MP.

The National Green Tribunal (NGT) has issued directives for the periodic monitoring of illegal sand mining and environmental violations in Tamia, Madhya Pradesh. This action was prompted by a news report, published in Patrika dated 18.12.2023 “Nadi — Nalo ka seena kiya chalni, dekhiye video ret ka avaidh khanan”, highlighting extensive illegal mining that is impacting rivers and lowering water levels.


The NGT formed a committee to investigate and instructed relevant authorities to monitor the area for these activities. Although an initial report by the State Pollution Control Board found no illegal mining, local residents reported recent occurrences. Consequently, the NGT has directed the State PCB, Regional Office, and Mining Officer to conduct regular monitoring and take appropriate action against violations, including prosecution and the collection of environmental compensation. The NGT has since closed the application after issuing these orders.

Justice Achal Kumar Paliwal dismissed a criminal revision petition challenging the conviction of a petitioner under Section 379 IPC for illegally transporting sand without a license. Despite some prosecution witnesses turning hostile, the Court found key testimony reliable and noted the petitioner failed to produce any license or proof of lawful mining. Emphasizing the environmental impact of illegal sand mining and the lack of evidence suggesting false implication, the Court upheld the conviction and one-year sentence imposed by the Trial and Appellate Courts, rejecting the plea for acquittal or a reduced sentence based on time already served.

The Central Zone Bench of the NGT, Bhopal took suo motu action based on a news report about illegal sand mining in the Son River in Umaria and Shahdol districts, Madhya Pradesh.


This mining poses a serious threat to the endangered Gharial (Gavialis gangeticus), a native crocodilian species known for its long snout and sharp teeth.


Key NGT directions (issued by Justice Dalip Singh and Dr. S.S. Garbayal, based on a pending case and media report submitted by advocate Nityanand Mishra):

- Immediate action by the District Collectors of Umaria and Shahdol.

- Seizure of equipment and vehicles used in illegal sand mining.

- Illegal bridge built across the river (blocking water flow) must be removed, and natural water flow restored.

- Pollution Control Board must obtain a factual report from its regional officer.

- The State's counsel must also submit reports from the Collectors and District Mining Officers of both districts.

The Madhya Pradesh government has reportedly initiated a move to denotify parts of Chambal and Son Gharial Sanctuaries in Morena and Sidhi districts to permit sand mining, following persistent illegal extraction and violence. Forest officials stated that the areas considered for denotification show no recent gharial breeding, and maps are being prepared for the State Wildlife Advisory Board; however, Supreme Court approval is required for the process.It was reported that a January 14 NGT order highlighted changes in the Son river’s course, with some dry stretches where mining might be feasible if denotified. Officials also mentioned the use of fly ash from Sidhi as a sand substitute. The forest department cited ongoing threats and attacks on staff, including the murder of a head constable on April 6 by mafia-backed youths. A PIL filed at the Gwalior High Court claimed that 200–300 trucks and dumpers of sand are illegally mined daily. Investigations revealed that unemployed local youth have taken to illegal mining, buying dumpers on bank loans with monthly installments reportedly as high as Rs 1.5 lakh.

35-year-old Sandeep Sharma was fatally run over by a dumper. He had previously gone to the police with complaints of threat to his life after he had done a sting operation exposing a police officer taking bribes from the sand mining mafia. The sting operation that he did showed a police officer taking bribes from the mafia.


Meanwhile, the district SP has constituted an SIT (Special Investigation Team) to probe the matter.

The Central Zone Bench of the NGT has directed the Madhya Pradesh state authorities to take urgent steps for the conservation of the Son Gharial Wildlife Sanctuary, located in Sidhi district, Madhya Pradesh. The river involved is the Son River, particularly a 200 km stretch within which the Gharial sanctuary lies. The case began with a 2014 application by Adv. Nityanand Mishra, highlighting unregulated illegal sand mining in the Son River, harming the endangered Gharial. The Forest Department allegedly failed to act, and RTI replies confirmed no valid mining sanctions were in place. The NGT noted a 96–98% decline in Gharial population as per IUCN data, and emphasized that it is a protected species under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972. A high-level Committee was constituted to prepare an action plan to check illegal mining and conserve the species. Members included: Indian Institute of Forest Management (Bhopal), Wildlife Institute of India (Dehradun), Indian School of Mines (Dhanbad), MoEF & CC, The District Administration was instructed to provide police support for enforcement in the sanctuary area. 


Compliance & Follow-Up:

- The Committee submitted its report late (Feb 2019 instead of Oct 2018).

- The NGT criticized the report for lacking detail on actual progress or enforcement, calling it a mere status update.

- The MP Government has now been ordered to ensure that all relevant departments listed in the Committee’s report file separate progress reports within 3 weeks.

- The Chief Wildlife Warden of MP has been directed to be present in person for the next hearing on 10th October 2019.

description:
The Madhya Pradesh government has approved amendments to the 2019 sand mining rules, introducing a new policy for the disposal of sand clusters across 44 districts. Under this policy, sand clusters will be auctioned through an e-tender-cum-auction process, with contracts awarded for a period of three years, extendable by two years. 


The State Mining Corporation will handle necessary permissions, and contractors are required to deposit 50% of the total cost in advance. Additionally, the contract amount will be payable monthly, with a 10% annual increase. This move aims to streamline sand mining operations and prevent contractors from abandoning projects midway.

The Special Investigation Team  reported to the National Green Tribunal  that 74% of sand mines in Narsinghpur district, located along the Narmada River, are violating environmental regulations. Out of 23 operational mines, 17 were found non-compliant. The Pollution Control Board took action by initiating sub-judice cases against five operators, ordering the closure of crushers at three sites, and issuing show-cause notices to nine others for continuing illegal mining. The mines involved include operators from areas such as Pipariya, Dharampuri, Gangai, Budhgaon, Jamunia, Kareli Kala, and others. Following the NGT’s directives, police have been deployed to monitor these sites. The next hearing is scheduled for September 2, 2016.

In Madhya Pradesh’s Guna district, the administration launched a major crackdown on illegal sand mining, seizing over 20 vehicles, including dumpers and tractors, used for transporting illegally mined sand. The raids were conducted in Bhamavad village - Kumbhraj tehsil, Barkhedi village - Guna tehsil, Dhimrayai village, and Laharghat.


The operation was led by senior officials from the revenue, police, and mining departments, targeting hotspots along riverbanks. Authorities have also initiated legal action against those involved. The district administration emphasised its commitment to curbing illegal mining, which poses environmental and legal challenges. Regular monitoring and joint operations are planned to prevent further violations and protect natural resources in the region.

Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) N.A. Gaud, and Sub-divisional Officer of Police (SDOP) faced firing from illegal sand mining people in the Chandipati village, Ajaygarh block, of Panna district. Former dacoit Kuber Singh who does cross-border transport of sand into Uttar Pradesh was named as the accused. It was the third attack in the week. Congress alleges the direct involvement of Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chauhan and his entire Cabinet. AICC General Secretary Digvijay Singh asked for an independent inquiry into illegal mining along with his party's 10 year rule prior. He expressed his discontent with the State Lokayukta and pointed out the mutually beneficial relationship between Chattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh. The police initially prima facie stated the invovlement of the mafia and have now denied making that link. State Congress was set to meet P M Chidambaram soon.

In a suo moto application initiated based on a news item published in Patrika, dated 18.12.2023 titles 'Nadi - Nalo ka seena kiya chalni, dekhiye video ret ka avaidh khanan' - a division bench directed the concerned authorities to monitor the area periodically for illegal mining activities and environmental violations.

district: Jabalpur, Alirajpur, Ashoknagar, Balaghat, Barwani, Anuppur, Betul, Burhanpur, Chhatarpur, Chhindwara, Bhopal, Damoh, Dewas, Dhar, Guna, Khandwa (East Nimar), Gwalior, Harda, Narmadapuram, Dindori, Indore, Jhabua, Katni, Mandla, Datia, Mandsaur, Morena, Narsimhapur, Neemuch, Bhind, Panna, Sehore, Shahdol, Shajapur, Seoni, Sheopur, Shivpuri, Sidhi, Singrauli, Satna, Tikamgarh, Vidisha, Khargone (West Nimar), Umaria, Niwari, Pandhurna, Mauganj, Sagar, Rewa, Ratlam, Ujjain, Rajgarh, Maihar, Raisen, Agar-Malwa
description:
The Madhya Pradesh Pollution Control Board had made environmental clearance mandatory for all sand mining operations statewide. This order, dated September 19 (2013), applied to every sand mining lease regardless of size, following a NGT directive on August 5, which required environmental clearance based on a Supreme Court order from February. The MP government had petitioned the Supreme Court seeking exemption for leases under five acres, arguing that the order would hurt the construction industry and conflict with the MP Mines and Mineral Rules, 1996. However, the NGT upheld the environmental clearance requirement, denying relief to the state.

Despite this, reports of rampant illegal sand mining persisted in rivers like the Narmada, Chambal, and Son, with allegations of large-scale illegal mining in Hoshangabad. RTI activist Ajay Dubey revealed that over the past five years, more than 3,000 illegal mining cases had been registered in MP, with many more likely unreported. MPPCB officials confirmed adherence to the 2013 environmental notification, which was expected to impact thousands of licensees but help protect the rivers.

In Madhya Pradesh’s Chambal region, the sand mafia has instilled deep fear among locals, officials, and even the police. Illegal sand mining, driven by high demand from construction, has flourished despite Supreme Court bans, especially along the Chambal River. The mafia operates with heavy machinery, armed guards, and political connections, often attacking officials who attempt to intervene. Forest officers report threats and violent resistance, while environmentalists warn of severe ecological damage to the Chambal Sanctuary, home to endangered species like gharials. The unchecked operations highlight a breakdown in law enforcement and rising influence of criminal networks in the region.


The report also mentions accounts of violence and deaths from past years.

In Betul district, Madhya Pradesh, the district in-charge minister, Narendra Shivaji Patel, has directed strict enforcement against the use of machines in sand mining operations. He emphasized that machine usage in sand mines is depriving local laborers of employment opportunities. The minister instructed that mining activities should comply with regulations, ensuring that contractors are not adversely affected and that rural employment is not hindered. He warned that any violations of mining rules would result in strict action against the offenders.

After the murder of a Patwari and Add. Sub Inspector by the sand mafia, the state government launched an 18-hour-long operation in Betul against illegal mining in which sand worth 20 crores was confiscated along with 31 dumpers and 8 Poclain machines. One FIR was also registered. The raids took place in 4 places - Dendupur, Pasaimal, Cheemdi, and Guwadi, after a complaint of illegal mining was received from Paasemal. The team found illegal mining pits on some parts of the area across the Tawa river and these pits were also inspected and measured. The article mentions that based on eyewitness accounts, cases have been registered against Deepesh Patel, Ravindra Chauhan, Pradeep Dubey and others.

The Alirajpur district administration had cracked down on illegal sand mining by raiding two sand storage and refining plants near the MP-Gujarat border on July 10, 2013. These plants, located in the Sakdi Faliya area near the Khandwa-Baroda state highway under Chandpur police station, were found storing premium quality sand worth several lakhs, destined for Mumbai and other parts of Maharashtra. The sand was sourced from two mines in Agal Gota and Chandpur, about 4 km from the plants.

The raid was conducted by a team led by Alirajpur district collector N P Dehria and Superintendent of Police Akhilesh Jha. Dehria confirmed that although sand mining had been permitted recently in Agal Gota and Chandpur, the sand was being illegally stored and refined before being sent out of state.

Investigations revealed that relatives of Congress leader Badhu Pachaya, reportedly close to state Congress president Kantilal Bhuria, held stakes in the mines supplying the sand. Badhu Pachaya arrived at the site following news of the raid.

river: Parvati, Kali Sindh, Nevaj, Narmada, Tawa, Chambal, Ajnar, Gadnala
description: In Madhya Pradesh’s Rajgarh district, unchecked illegal sand mining is threatening local rivers like the Parvati and Kalisindh. Despite regulations, mining continues openly, damaging river ecosystems, altering natural flow, and increasing erosion. Locals allege that trucks operate day and night under the protection of political and administrative collusion. The Parvati river, a key water source, is especially vulnerable. Authorities have taken limited action, and environmental concerns remain largely unaddressed. The ongoing mining not only endangers biodiversity but also jeopardises long-term water security for surrounding communities dependent on these rivers.

In a tragic incident, at least three persons including a woman and her son were killed and three others sustained injuries during sand mining for the construction of a temple in the village in Madhya Pradesh's Jabalpur district on Wednesday. Additional Superintendent of Police Suryakant Sharma said that the incident took place on the river bank at Katra Ramkhiriya village.

district: Narmadapuram, Alirajpur, Anuppur, Dindori, Mandla, Balaghat, Seoni, Jabalpur, Narsimhapur, Chhindwara, Betul, Harda, Raisen, Sehore, Khandwa (East Nimar), Khargone (West Nimar), Dewas, Indore, Dhar, Barwani
description:
A day after imposing a blanket ban on sand mining from the Narmada riverbed, the Madhya Pradesh government set up a committee on May 23, 2017, to advise on scientific mining practices. The panel, led by state mining and industries minister Rajendra Shukla, included senior bureaucrats and technical experts from institutions like IIT Roorkee, IIT Kharagpur, and Barkatullah University. The committee was tasked with recommending processes, criteria, and modern techniques for sustainable and transparent sand mining, aiming to protect the river and environment.


While the cabinet acknowledged that the mining ban could cause an annual revenue loss of Rs 200 crore, it emphasized the importance of safeguarding the Narmada river and controlling ecological damage. The committee was expected to submit its initial report within six months, with decisions likely by September or October. The government also banned mechanized mining in other rivers to conserve their ecology, citing misuse of mining leases by companies causing environmental harm.


Note: Exact districts are not mentioned, hence all districts in MP through which the Narmada flows have been marked.

district: Indore, Ujjain, Ratlam, Mandsaur, Neemuch, Morena, Etawah, Agra, Kota, Baran, Bundi, Sawai Madhopur, Karauli
description: Illegal sand mining was reported to be severely threatening the ghariyal population in the Chambal sanctuary, which spans Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan. The sanctuary, covering 425 km of the Chambal river, is the primary habitat for these reptiles, which rely on sand banks for nesting and basking. Wildlife activist Upamanyu Raju filed a complaint with the National Green Tribunal (NGT) highlighting that illegal sand extraction, along with fishing and stone quarrying, was destroying ghariyal nests and disturbing their habitat.

The Son River in Madhya Pradesh, once rich in biodiversity, is facing ecological degradation due to rampant illegal sand mining, irregular water releases from the Bansagar Dam, and unauthorized constructions. These activities have led to severe soil erosion and a significant decline in the population of gharials within the Son Gharial Wildlife Sanctuary. The gharial population decreased from 72 in 2016 to just 20 (all female) in 2021. 


Despite a 2019 directive from the National Green Tribunal to halt illegal sand mining, such activities persist, often occurring at night. Additionally, the construction of a bridge at Jogdah, the only known breeding site for gharials in the sanctuary, poses further threats to their habitat. Experts warn that these disturbances could have lasting impacts on the gharial population and the overall health of the river ecosystem.

district: Mandla, Dindori, Shahdol, Dhar, Jhabua, Barwani, Jabalpur
description: Principal bench of Madhya Pradesh High Court at Jabalpur, on Tuesday, issued notices to chief secretary, principal secretary mining, principal secretary rural development, MD mining, collector Mandla and Jabalpur, and others over illegal sand mining and alleged violation of Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act(PESA Act) in Mandla district. The court has given four-week time to the respondents to reply. A PIL was filed at the Principal bench of the MPHC regarding illegal mining in six districts (primarily "Mandla" has been mentioned as it was led by Mandla Janpad vice president Sandeep Singore ) where application of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act has been found to be wanting and hence the mining contracts have been cited as being null and void.

In Madhya Pradesh, Health Minister Narendra Shivaji Patel stopped two sand-loaded dumpers near Harsili Toll Plaza in Raisen, suspecting them of being overloaded. He checked the documents and found the dumpers carrying more sand than permitted, leading to their seizure by the local police. However, the Mineral Department later contradicted the Minister's claim, stating that the sand quantity was within the legal limit as per their verification on the official portal. The incident has highlighted tensions between the government’s departments and raised concerns over the influence of the sand mafia in the state.

An assistant sub-inspector (ASI) has been crushed to death by a tractor-trolley used for transporting illegally mined sand in Madhya Pradesh's Shahdol district, a police official said on Sunday. 'Piloting' in Shahdol is used to refer to moving ahead a vehicle while seeing the road is clear and no checking is being done by authorities.

Two persons have been arrested in connection with the incident which took place on the intervening night of Saturday-Sunday in Badoli village under Beohari police station limits.

निहालगंज थाना पुलिस ने बुधवार को चम्बल रेत परिवहन कर रहे दो युवकों को गिरफ्तार किया। 


Two youths were arrested for illegally transporting sand from River Chambal. They were charged under the Wildlife Protection Act (WPA).

In Madhya Pradesh’s Khargone district, a mining officer filed an FIR against six journalists after they questioned him about alleged illegal sand mining activities. The reporters had approached the officer for a statement, following which he accused them of obstructing government work and threatening him. The journalists, however, claim they were only performing their duties and that the FIR is an attempt to intimidate the press and suppress reporting on illegal mining. The incident has drawn criticism from press bodies and the opposition, raising concerns over press freedom and accountability in addressing environmental and illegal mining issues.

An assistant sub-inspector, Mahendra Bagri, was fatally run over by a vehicle carrying illegally mined sand. Those accused are Raj Rawat (the tractor driver), Ashutosh Singh (piloting the tractor and also the son of the owner of the tractor), and Surendra Singh (the owner of the tractor). All have since been arrested, and the authorities also demolished the houses of Surendra Singh (valued at around rs. 10 lakh) and Raj Rawat (valued at around rs. 4 lakh). 


The report also mentions another death in the previous year (2024) of a revenue department officer (similar case of running a vehicle over in case of mining sand from Sone river) in Gopalpur, Shahdol district.

The sand mafia had reportedly constructed a bridge across the river in Panna district. This led to obstruction in the river flow, and the sub-divisional magistrate deployed a patwari and secretary of the panchayat to keep vigil after destroying the bridge twice.

district: Narmadapuram, Bhind, Morena, Shahdol, Betul, Harda, Dewas, Dhar
description:
Despite the NGT order, Sand mines have not been handover to contractors for the last eight months in Narmadapuram district. Three groups have 118 sand mines in Narmadapuram district. These mines could not be started due to lack of permission. Despite this, the sand mafia is removing sand from the Narmada River. This situation is worsened as state authorities are busy with national and state elections. In Narmadapuram district headquarters, illegal mining is taking place 24 hours in various locations such as Karbala-Kharraghat, Javali, Amkhedi Dongarwada, Barandua, Palaghat-Khazhanpur, Village Raipur, Malakhedi, Bandrabhan, Sangakheda Bridge, Nimsadia, Tawa Bridge including Babai, Semri, Semari, Sohagpur, Pipariya, Bankhedi, Dolria etc using Poclain machines. 


Under the instructions of Collector Sonia Meena, the Mineral Department and the police, took action in village Dimawar and Babri of Sivanimalwa and seized 18 motor boats after getting inputs of illegal excavation of sand by motorboats. Similarly, on May 17, a tractor trolley was seized by the Department of Minerals in Sohagpur for illegal transportation of sand.
N/A

Despite imposing a blanket ban on sand mining from the Narmada River, there have been sightings of trucks loaded with freshly mined sand from Babri Ghat of the Narmada River. Officials have denied any such happenings. Environmentalists have, however, also questioned the motives of the governments, stating that the ban says nothing about the illegal sand mining, which accounts for 70% of all mining.


There are also accusations placed on Shivraj Singh Chouhan (the Chief Minister), having family members/relatives in the mining business, and how they will profit immensely from the ban by being able to sell the sand they hoarded before the ban at exorbitant prices. The article concludes by stating this to be the case across the state, citing Khargone (specifically illegal mining at Kunda river) as an example.

In Dindori district, Madhya Pradesh, a joint operation by the police and mining department led to the seizure of four dumpers overloaded with illegally mined sand near Samnapur road. The vehicles, transporting sand from Kamko Mohania village to the district headquarters, lacked documentation for royalty payments. This action followed reports of ongoing illegal sand mining along the Dindori-Mandla border. Mining officer Shashank Shukla initiated the operation upon receiving a tip-off, resulting in the confiscation of the vehicles, which are now held at Dindori Kotwali police station. The incident has raised concerns about the effectiveness of local police in curbing illegal mining activities.

Madhya Pradesh police seized over 4,000 tonnes of illegally mined sand dumped at a farm in Morena district's Nagra village which was from the National Chambal Gharial Wildlife Sanctuary. The report mentions that 4 attacks have taken place on jawans by sand mafia which led the Gwalior bench of Bhopal High Court to order additional forces in and around the park. The report quotes a local resident working on mining issues saying that all who work in the industry are armed and dangerous. The drivers of the trucks and tractors drive recklessly causing accidents. It also mentions that the police have filed 23 cases against 600-odd people for illegal mining since 2012 in Morena district alone. The police, however, have arrested only 29 people.

The Madhya Pradesh government took disciplinary action against several police officials for their alleged involvement in or negligence towards illegal sand mining. In a major crackdown, 21 police personnel were transferred, including a Superintendent of Police, while departmental inquiries were launched against others. The action followed mounting evidence of police complicity or inaction in curbing rampant illegal mining, particularly along riverbanks. Chief Minister Kamal Nath's government aimed to send a strong message about zero tolerance for corruption and environmental violations. The crackdown highlights the deep-rooted nexus between the sand mafia and law enforcement in the state.

Villagers presented a list of complaints to their Zilla Panchayat Member in Shahdol district stating that illegal and uncurbed sand mining is leading to a loss of agriculture productivity and leading to fall in groundwater levels. They are worried about the situation worsening with uncurbed mining as it leads to less water in the water sources as well - such as ponds and lakes.  Hundreds of villagers including the Sarpanch of the Gram Panchayat were present during the memorandum.

In Narmadapuram (Hoshangabad) district, Madhya Pradesh, a Nayab Tehsildar was attacked by a group of individuals while en route to raid an illegal sand mining site. The official sustained injuries during the assault. Following the incident, authorities arrested 15 individuals in connection with the attack. The incident underscores the challenges faced by officials in curbing illegal sand mining activities in the region.

धौलपुर के सैंपऊ में कौलारी पुलिस और अवैध चंबल बजरी माफिया के बीच संघर्ष हुआ, जिसमें थाना प्रभारी को चोट लगी है.


A clash broke out between the Kaulari police and the illegal Chambal sand mafia in Sampu, Dholpur, in which the station in-charge was injured.

Three days after Harda district collector Srikant Bhanot was transferred to the state secretariat as deputy secretary, mining (May 24), the government cancelled the transfer order.

Bhanot will continue as Harda collector, replacing Tarun Rathi who had taken over temporarily.


The decision surprised political observers who link it to former minister Kamal Patel’s confrontation with the state government. Kamal Patel had highlighted illegal sand mining issues in Narmada and filed a petition with the National Green Tribunal, embarrassing the government.

Bhanot had taken strict action under the National Security Act, banning Patel’s son from Harda district, escalating tensions.

A BJP MLA, RD Prajapati, who represents Chandla assembly segment in Chhatarpur district, received life threatening call from sand mafia with them threatening to shoot him. The article mentions that Prajapati said he has been raising the issue of illegal sand mining in his area for a long time with villagers in his constituency live in constant fear because of sand mining mafia whose gunmen threaten and beat poor villagers. He filed a complaint with the local police, and went to meet the CM.

district: Dhar, Harda, Dewas, Sehore, Narsimhapur, Chhatarpur, Bhind, Narmadapuram, Mandla, Jabalpur
description: The sand mining syndicate has adopted a new way to evade the police, that is, by using jetties and boats to extract sand and transport it across districts. The police, not being equipped to boat or navigate the turbulent waters of the Narmada, can't do much even when they see boats transporting the sand. The penalty placed on violators of the Mining Act is hardly ever recovered, and although the registered complaints of illegal mining continue to increase, even the on-road vehicles seized continue to remain dismally low. Amidst all this, politicians and political parties are busy blaming each other.

district: Udupi, Kalaburagi / Gulbarga, Shivamogga / Shimoga, Raichur
description:
Karnataka’s 2021 sand policy aims to streamline sand supply and pricing, cut corruption, and involve local bodies, but skips focus on environmental safeguards.


Sand extraction has begun in Udupi and Kundapur from CRZ rivers like Varahi, Swarna, Sita, and Sauparnika.


Extraction is allowed in non-CRZs and by sea divers in CRZs without machines; more blocks in Karkala may open soon.


Local sand is priced at Rs 300/ton by gram panchayats; urban supply from riverbeds costs Rs 700/ton.


Mysuru Mines and Hutti Gold Mines are authorised to extract sand; 50% of royalties go to panchayats.


Panchayats can issue permits, raising concerns over enforcement, local politics, and bribery.


District Sand Committees will meet every two months to manage leases and permits.


Illegal sand mining is still reported, especially in Kundapur, from unapproved sand dunes.


Supporters say the policy empowers local bodies and may reduce illegal mining; critics say it increases corruption.


Experts say the policy prioritizes construction over conservation and ignores CRZ, eco-sensitive, and buffer zone rules.


Karnataka faces a yearly 15–20 lakh tonne sand shortage; M-sand is underused despite potential.


Inter-state transport is banned, but illegal sand flow to Kerala continues.

The Sidhi police has taken action against nearly 50 police personnel by either suspending them, instituting departmental inquiry against them or removing them from service in the last two months. 


In one instance, the entire police outpost in Piparohar comprising 16 personnel, headed by a sub-inspector was changed, when the higher-ups found that the entire outpost was involved in abetting illegal sand mining.


Interestingly, the police at the time of this report getting published mentioned that they had registered over 100 cases in the preceding 2 months, and that they have also started charging this illegality as theft under Section 379 of the IPC.

मुरैना में दो स्थानों पर 90 ट्रॉली अवैध चंबल रेत नष्ट की गई. बताया गया कि करीब 17 लाख का बालू नष्ट हो गया. पहली कार्रवाई झुंडपुरा अस्पताल के पास और दूसरी मुरैना-आगरा रोड से देवगढ़ थाने की ओर नहर किनारे की गई।


(Raid on two locations in Morena district (Jhundpura - near Jhundpur hospital and Devgarh - on Morena-Agra road towards Devgarh police station), resulted in the destruction of 90 trolleys and 17 lakh rupees.)

district: Morena, Dhaulpur, Gwalior, Bhind, Bharatpur, Agra, Etawah, Jhansi
description:
ग्वालियर चम्बल की सबसे बड़ी और साफ पानी की नदी चंबल के अस्तित्व को खतरा पैदा हो गया है। वजह है नदी के मुहानों से रेत का अवैध खनन। अदालत और नेशनल ग्रीन ट्रिब्यूनल (एनजीटी) की रोक के बावजूद चंबल से रेत का अवैध खनन जारी है। ऐसे में चंबल के अस्तित्व को तो खतरा है ही, इससे आसपास का पर्यावरणीय संतुलन भी बिगड़ने के कगार पर है। अवैध रेत खनन से यहां बनाई गई घड़ियाल और डॉल्फिन सेंचुरी के अस्तित्व को खतरा है। 


The existence of Chambal, the biggest and cleanest river of Gwalior, is in danger. The reason is illegal mining of sand from the mouth of the river. Despite the ban by the court and the National Green Tribunal (NGT), illegal mining of sand from Chambal continues. In such a situation, not only the existence of Chambal is in danger, but the environmental balance of the surrounding area is also on the verge of deteriorating. The existence of the Gharial and Dolphin Sanctuary built here is in danger due to illegal sand mining.

रिपोर्ट में मंदसौर में चंबल नदी पर हो रहे अवैध रेत खनन (सक्शन पंप, उत्खनन यंत्र, विशाल नौकाएं, ट्रैक्टर जैसी मशीनों का उपयोग करके) का उल्लेख किया गया है, जिससे नदी नष्ट हो रही है। खान एवं खनिज विभाग खनन रोकने के लिए पर्याप्त कार्रवाई नहीं कर रहा है।


(The report mentions about the illegal sand mining taking place (use of machines like suction pumps, excavators, huge boats, tractors) on and destroying the Chambal river in Mandsaur. The mines and minerals department is not taking adequate action to stop the mining. )

चंबल नदी से अवैध रेत परिवहन का मामला सामने आया है. बताया जा रहा है कि सुबह होते ही जिला मुख्यालय के चारों तरफ अवैध रेत की मंडी लग जाती है. बड़ोखर चौराहे पर लगी मंडी पर स्टेशन रोड थाना प्रभारी ने अवैध रेत से भरे 4 ट्रैक्टर ट्रालियों को चालक सहित पकड़ लिया. वहीं, 4 ट्रैक्टर ट्राली भागने में कामयाब हो गए.


A case of illegal sand transportation from the Chambal River has come to light. It is being reported that illegal sand markets are set up around the district headquarters as soon as morning arrives. At the market at Barokhar intersection, the Station Road police station in-charge seized four tractor trolleys filled with illegal sand, along with their drivers. However, four tractor trolleys managed to escape.

डीएसटी टीम एवं कोतवाली थाना पुलिस ने मंगलवार को आईसीएल फैक्ट्री के पास जंगल में बजरी माफियाओं के ठिकाने पर बड़ी कार्रवाई को अंजाम दिया है. 800 ट्रॉली से अधिक बजरी भंडारण को पुलिस ने पकड़ा है. बुलडोजर एवं ट्रैक्टर-ट्रॉलियों से बजरी को जब्त करने की कार्रवाई की जा रही है.


(The DST team and the Kotwali police station carried out a major operation against a gravel mafia hideout in the forest near the ICL factory. Police seized over 800 trolleys of gravel. Bulldozers and tractor-trolleys are being used to seize the gravel.)

मनियां थाना पुलिस ने कार्रवाई करते हुए अवैध चम्बल बजरी का परिवहन करते हुए एक ट्रेलर को जब्त कर चालक को गिरफ्तार किया है। माफिया के लोग ट्रेलर पर गिट्टी बिछाकर अवैध रूप से चंबल बजरी का परिवहन कर रहे थे।


Maniyan police seized a trailer transporting illegally mined sand from the Chambal, and arrested the driver. Mafia members were illegally transporting the sand by hiding it under a layer of gravel on the trailer, when transporting the sand from Dholpur to Agra.

धौलपुर पुलिस ने अवैध चंबल बजरी से भरे ट्रैक्टर-ट्रॉली समेत एक आरोपी को गिरफ्तार किया है। आरोपी पर बीएनएस की धारा 303(2), वन्यजीव संरक्षण अधिनियम की धारा 29/52, वन अधिनियम की धारा 41 और 42 के तहत मामला दर्ज किया गया था।


Dholpur police have arrested an accused along with a tractor-trolley loaded with illegal Chambal gravel. The accused was booked under BNS section 303(2), section 29/52 under wildlife protection act, section 41, 42 under forest act.

राजस्थान के धौलपुर में पुलिस ने चंबल नदी से अवैध रूप से रेत निकालने के लिए नए-नए तरीके अपना रहे दो ट्रकों को पकड़ा है। ये ट्रक भारी मात्रा में अवैध रूप से निकाली गई रेत से भरे हुए थे और उसे छोटे पत्थरों और बजरी से ढक रहे थे।

Speaking at a national seminar on crocodile conservation, he explained that sand mining, along with dam construction and loss of nesting habitats, has significantly disrupted crocodile ecosystems.

In lieu of this, the collector (Shrikant Pandey) issued notice to the concerned party, in this case Digiana Industries Private Limited, asking why fines (both compounding and non-compounding), totalling to INR 300 crores , should not be imposed. The party was given 7 days to reply. As per the news report, the company's director had disputed the charges.

The Karnataka government has clarified that it is not allowing sand mining but is proposing controlled removal of sandbars from the Sharavathi, Kali, Aghanashini and Gangavali rivers in Uttara Kannada. This response was submitted to the National Green Tribunal following complaints of illegal sand mining. The government has applied for clearance from the State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA), and work will begin only after approval. Officials said sandbar accumulation can block river flow, cause bank erosion, and increase flood risk. The proposed removals aim to protect river channels while following environmental safeguards and benefiting local communities.

Illegal sand mining along the Brahmaputra River has intensified in the Jarabari–Panikhaiti stretch of Palasbari in Assam, raising serious environmental and safety concerns. Heavy machinery such as JCBs and dumpers is reportedly being used daily to extract sand in violation of existing norms. The unscientific excavation has altered the river’s natural flow, threatening aquatic life, wildlife habitats, and nearby embankments. Local residents fear increased erosion, flooding, and damage to roads and farmland, especially during the monsoon. Authorities, including forest officials, are accused of inaction despite the visible mining activity. Villagers have demanded immediate intervention and strict action to prevent a potential environmental disaster.

The Enforcement Directorate (ED) raided places all throughout Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh as part of an investigation into illegal sand mining and money laundering. The raid was carried out in multiple locations across both the state (Saoner, Khapa, Bhopal, Hoshangabad, etc.) linked to many traders and political figures, including a Shiv Sena (UBT) leader. The investigation is being carried out under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), backed up by the inputs from earlier illegal mining cases.

A 53-year-old man was arrested by Pernambut Police near Gudiyatham town, Vellore, for illegal sand mining in dry sites of the Palar River. The farmer, along with his partner(who fled from the site), was transporting the sand via a bullock cart, meant for sale to the private builders. A probe for the case is underway.

Around 10 p.m., an inter-state task group led by the NGT raided illicit sand mining along the Yamuna near Harampur and Jagatpur (Delhi–UP boundary). They took three excavators that were working 7 km inside Delhi with false permits for Pachera (Ghaziabad) and a 2 km illegal transport route. Since October, five drives in Navraspur–Pachera–Loni led to seizures and two FIRs. An NGT panel also pointed out GRAP-3 violations, night mining, and other environmental infractions in Navraspur.

The report highlights the fearlessness of the "sand mafias" towards law and police officials. 3 major attacks in Sheopur, including an incident of stone pelting on government officials took place, and the vehicles of the Forest Department were also attacked. A sand-laden dumper was confiscated, but later it was removed from the site forcefully by the operators. In another incident, a tractor-trolley loaded with soil crushed a mother and son riding a bike. The son died on the spot in the tragic accident, while the mother was seriously injured.

Police in Shahdol district, Madhya Pradesh, tore down the homes of two people who were charged with the illegal sand mining-related death of ASI Mahendra Bagri. He was driven over by a tractor full of sand while on patrol in Badoli village at night (Beohari police station area). Police detained Raj Rawat, the tractor driver, and Surendra Singh, the tractor owner, along with his son Ashutosh Singh. Authorities have filed a FIR for murder and unlawful sand mining, and they want to send the suspects away. The state administration has also suggested that the family of the officer who died get ₹1 crore in compensation.

The Supreme Court of India decided to hear a case brought by journalists from Madhya Pradesh who say they were attacked by police because they were reporting on illicit sand mining activities linked to the "sand mafia." On Monday, the case was set for a hearing. The court asked about procedural concerns and why the petitioners hadn't gone to the Madhya Pradesh High Court first. They also agreed to send notifications to the state government in the case.

description: A study by Presidency University, with the support of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, reveals the severe impact of sand mining on the environment in West Bengal's rivers, particularly in the Rarh region. The study utilises satellite images to demonstrate that the Ajay, Damodar, and Subarnarekha rivers have numerous hollows and pools in their riverbeds. It also shows that sand mining changes the shape of the rivers and causes additional challenges. They found a lot of fresh landscapes that are distinct from the ones we regularly see.

Large-scale illegal sand mining is taking place in the Sharada River catchment area within Chodavaram mandal limits at Gavaravaram, Shemunapalli, Gajapatinagaram, Juttada, and Muddhurti villages of Visakhapatnam district of Andhra Pradesh despite government's orders that free sand should only be for local use, not commercial purposes. Sand mafias are conducting auctions in villages and extracting large quantities of sand at night using excavators, then transporting it to Visakhapatnam and other areas. Loads of 20 tons are sold for Rs. 15,000-20,000. Despite complaints from Jana Sena leaders, Revenue and Mining department officials are either ignoring the situation or actively cooperating with illegal operators. Task Force committees formed to stop the mining exist only on paper and are not functioning in practice. Locals say only direct intervention by the District Collector will stop this illegal activity.

Rampant illegal sand mining business is being conducted in the Chithravathi River near Amadaguru and Obuladevicheruvu mandals in Sri Satya Sai and Ananthapuramu districts. Around 25 tractors are regularly parked near Mohammedabad cross village of Ananthapuramu (dt.) to extract sand illegally. Local villagers and farmers are worried that this mining will cause their borewells to dry up. Tahsildar Ramanatha Reddy has stated that action will be taken against unauthorized sand transporters.

A former YSRCP minister has accused ruling party leaders in Andhra Pradesh of facilitating round-the-clock illegal sand mining in the Penna riverbed. The minister presented photographic evidence showing sand excavation inside the riverbed at Virivuru and Surayapalem villages in Podalakuru Mandal, SPSR Nellore district. The mining has allegedly blocked irrigation canals, damaged the river ecosystem, and created dangerous pits that have caused fatalities. Those who challenge the sand mafia allegedly face threats and attacks, while police remain inactive and reportedly seek ministerial approval before taking action instead of enforcing the law.

description: This article talks about sand mining has increased over the last few years within rivers of West Bengal. It explains how mining alters rivers' appearance, functioning and ecological character. It has the potential to change the channel geomorphology and stability, inducing riverbank erosion, and altering in-stream habitats for aquatic flora and fauna. Their study found increased turbidity and poos dissolved oxygen levels in parts of rivers where mining took place. Earlier miners were active in the river Damodar and the Ajay, but recently mining has started in rivers like Subarnarekha, which was quite pristine earlier.

JD(S) MLA Karemma Nayak was confronted and threatened by sand miners from Devadurga after she raised the issue of rampant illegal sand mining in the Krishna riverbed of Raichur district of Karnataka during the Legislative Assembly session. She reported that farmers are concerned about damage to their crops and women feel unsafe venturing outside due to the mafia's activities. Home Minister G. Parameshwara acknowledged that the problem extends beyond Devadurga across the entire state. A complaint has been filed against the sand mafia for threatening the MLA.

This article talks about the mafia nexus operating on the Ajay rivers and it's adjoining tributaries. It details how locals are trapped in digging rivers, because of monetary benefits. It details out the involvement of local police and the overall political nexus. Government maintains that it's policy will somehow work on the ground but it's not showing any effect.

Karnataka HC division bench has initiated suo motu proceedings to probe into the allegations on rampant illegal sand mining in the state. This was in cognisance to the Home Minister's and Devadurga MLA's recent statements in assembly about influential people being involved in such activities. The news reports referred  to by the court mentioned sand mining from the Krishna river basin at night as farmers reported deposition of sand on their crops and a woman MLA from Raichur district complained about receiving threat to her life from the people involved in mining. The court issued notice to the state government and directed to file a response within three weeks.

The Phillaur police have initiated legal action under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, following a complaint filed by the Junior Mining Inspector of Jalandhar district against a resident of village Awa for illegal sand mining near the Sutlej riverbed. The sand was allegedly being extracted under the pretext of soil excavation work near Selkiana village in Ludhiana district and subsequently transported to Jalandhar district.

Minister Aidal Kansana's remark "There's no sand mafia, rather they are paet (stomach) mafia & I'm in their support" is getting viral country-wide.


This was during a press conference was held regarding the state government's budget. Minister Kansana described the budget as a path to prosperity for the poor, youth, and farmers. The journalists asked questions about the legalization of sand mining in the Chambal River.

After the news was published in Dainik Bhaskar Digital regarding illegal sand mining in Rajghat of Morena, the administration is in action mode. During the raid joint team of revenue, police and forest department destroyed the sand (estimated to be around Rs 30 lakh) that was illegally dumped at Rajghat. There must have been more than a thousand trolleys of sand. The temporary pathways created to access river banks destroyed by digging trenches.

Led by the Forest Department and police, the operation used six JCBs, deployed 250 police personnel, blocked illegal access routes, and created panic among the sand mafia.

चंबल नदी के राजघाट पर रेत माफिया का कब्जा हो गया है, जहां वन विभाग ने पर्यटन केंद्र बनाया है। मुख्यमंत्री डॉ. मोहन यादव ने हाल ही में इस स्थान की सराहना की थी, लेकिन अब यहां रेत का अवैध खनन जोरों पर है। वन विभाग के अधिकारी राजनीतिक संरक्षण का आरोप लगा रहे हैं और कार्रवाई की मांग कर रहे हैं।


On February 17th itself, Chief Minister Dr. Yadav, the Assembly Speaker, and others released 10 gharials at Jaitpur Ghat, barely a kilometer from Rajghat. LUCKNOW: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav, on Wednesday, accused UP government-led officials of illegal mining and environmental destruction in the ravines of Chambal in his native district of Etawah.


Residents reported unauthorised soil mining and hill levelling activities continuing for two to three months, with heavy machines operating round the clock. Consequently, a flattening of a 70 -80-metre-high mud mound was reported affecting over 20,000 to 30,000 square feet of terrain. However, local sources suggested that the activity could be related to some residential development plans.

The ASI alleged that he was being mentally harassed by the cops led by Godan police station in-charge Arvind Singh Bhadauria, since he stopped the tractor trolley loaded with illegally mined sand of sand mafia Babloo Yadav.

In the video, two constables posted at the Chinnouni police station are seen standing on the river bank, allowing tractors loaded with illegal sand to cross their border. Based on this, the Superintendent of Police (SP) has ordered the immediate suspension of both constables.


It is rumored that the police charge the sand mafia 5,000 rupees as entry fees for each tractor carrying sand for a month. After that, the sand mafia openly trades illegal sand in broad daylight.

The potential environmental impact is also scary as already the water flow in parts of the Tungabhadra River has reportedly dwindled to a trickle due to excessive sand removal.

Deputy Commissioner Aditya Uppal said he would examine the matter, while a Mining Department official claimed ignorance of the activity. Last year's severe floods in the area, which displaced families and submerged farmland, were partly attributed to illegal mining. The NGT had imposed the ban following a petition by Gahlri village panchayat, but enforcement remains weak.
